BNY.company: Bank of New York Mellon Corp
BNY.brief: The Bank of New York Mellon Corp filed an 8-K announcing a 19% increase in its quarterly cash dividend from $0.53 to $0.63 per share, expected to commence in Q3 2026 pending board approval. The filing also notes that the company's Stress Capital Buffer remains at the 2.5% floor following the 2026 Fed stress test, and that it continues to be authorized for share repurchases under an existing program announced in April 2026. Repurchases may occur via open market, private transactions, or structured programs. No advisor or recommendation is noted. This is a shareholder return event, not a merger or acquisition. Watch for dividend declaration and actual buyback execution.

HLX.brief: Helix Energy Solutions Group filed Amendment No. 1 to its S-4 registration statement in connection with its proposed merger with Hornbeck Offshore Services under the Agreement and Plan of Merger dated April 22, 2026. The transaction structure involves Odyssey Sub, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Helix, merging with Hornbeck. Terms include a stock-for-stock consideration; exact exchange ratio, premium, and implied value are not stated in the filing excerpt. Helix's board recommends the transaction; Baker Botts and Kirkland & Ellis serve as legal advisors. The merger is subject to regulatory approval and shareholder votes. Risk-arb investors should monitor SEC effectiveness and shareholder meeting timing for closing mechanics.

MPWR.brief: Monolithic Power Systems filed an 8-K reporting its 2026 annual meeting voting results and declared a regular quarterly cash dividend of $2.00 per share. The dividend will be paid on July 15, 2026, to shareholders of record as of June 30, 2026. This is a routine capital return event with no premium, merger, or activist involvement. The company is returning capital to shareholders in the ordinary course. No special situation or extraordinary corporate event is present. Watch for any future changes in dividend policy or special dividends.

SWKS.brief: Skyworks Solutions filed an 8-K reporting results of early participation in its exchange offers and consent solicitations for Qorvo's outstanding 4.375% Senior Notes due 2029 and 3.375% Senior Notes due 2031. The filing is an update to a previously disclosed exchange offer as part of a merger agreement. No terms (price, premium, close date) are stated in this filing. The company is the issuer offering to exchange its securities for Qorvo notes. The structural detail is that this relates to a merger integration step. Watch for final exchange results and merger closing conditions; risk-arb focuses on successful exchange and shareholder approvals.

TYL.brief: Tyler Technologies disclosed entry into a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan to repurchase up to $150 million of its common stock from June 16 to July 30, 2026, as part of a $1.0 billion board-authorized repurchase program (February 3, 2026) with $332.7 million remaining. The plan is prearranged and complies with Rule 10b5-1 to allow repurchases even if material non-public information arises. Funding comes from cash and credit facility; no premium, tender, or structural changes. Watch for execution pace and impact on shares outstanding; no risk-arb angle as this is an open-market buyback.

ADSK.brief: Autodesk filed an 8-K to disclose the establishment of a $2.0 billion unsecured commercial paper program on July 13, 2026. The program allows issuance of notes with maturities up to 365 days, backstopped by an existing $2.0 billion revolving credit facility. Proceeds will fund general corporate purposes, including partial financing for the previously announced acquisition of MaintainX Inc. per the May 28, 2026 merger agreement. No notes have been issued yet. This event is routine financing, not a standalone special situation. Watch for any future issuer delays or market conditions affecting note placement.

ENSG.brief: Ensign Group filed an 8-K disclosing a $60 million increase to its existing $40 million stock repurchase program, bringing total authorization to $100 million. The program allows open-market or privately negotiated repurchases under Rule 10b-18 and 10b5-1 plans. No price per share, premium, or expiration date was specified; repurchases are discretionary based on market conditions and liquidity. The board approved the increase on June 12, 2026, with no advisor named. The filing is a capital-return event, signaling management's view of undervaluation. Watch for actual buyback pace and potential EPS accretion as risk-arb angles.

FOXA.brief: Fox Corp disclosed entry into a $1.0 billion senior unsecured term loan facility on June 30, 2026, to partially fund its acquisition of Roku, Inc., which was announced on June 15, 2026, per a June 14 merger agreement. The facility, with Morgan Stanley as administrative agent, matures two years post-closing and includes an accordion feature for up to $1.0 billion in additional term loans. Interest rates are based on Base Rate or Term SOFR plus margins tied to Fox's credit ratings. The filing provides financing details; no premium or other terms for the Roku acquisition were stated. The closing is contingent on customary conditions; watch for regulatory approval progress.

IIPR.brief: Innovative Industrial Properties Inc., through its operating partnership, issued $402.5 million aggregate principal amount of 6.00% exchangeable senior notes due 2029 in a private placement under Rule 144A. The offering included full exercise of a $52.5 million greenshoe option. The notes are senior unsecured obligations guaranteed by the company, ranking equal with other unsecured debt. Proceeds may be used for general corporate purposes including capital returns. Interest is payable semiannually. Watch for future use of proceeds—if directed toward share buybacks or dividends, this would be a classic capital-return event.

KIM.brief: Kimco Realty OP, LLC filed an 8-K on June 15, 2026, solely to disclose the entry into a material definitive agreement for a preferred stock issuance. The filing details the terms of depositary shares representing 7.250% Class N Cumulative Convertible Perpetual Preferred Stock, along with Class L and Class M Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock. No specific price per share, premium, or conversion terms are provided in the excerpt. The agreement creates a direct financial obligation and an unregistered sale of equity securities. This is a routine capital-raising transaction through preferred equity, not a special situation. No advisors or board recommendations are noted, and the focus is on the operational funding of the REIT. Monitor for future pricing and conversion details.

TLN.brief: Talen Energy Corp filed an 8-K reporting the consummation of its acquisition of three natural gas power plants (Lawrenceburg 1,120 MW, Waterford 875 MW, Darby 456 MW) from Energy Capital Partners affiliates. The purchase price was $3.45 billion, consisting of ~$2.55 billion cash and 2,399,998 shares of common stock. The deal closed on June 15, 2026, with acquired entities expected to guarantee Talen's existing debt. No board recommendation or advisors are named in this excerpt. The acquisition was previously announced on January 15, 2026. Watch for integration execution and potential earnings accretion from the added 2,451 MW of gas-fired generation.

BANR.brief: Banner Corp filed an amended S-4 registration statement for its merger with Pacific Financial Corp. Under the agreement dated April 30, 2026, Pacific Financial will merge into Banner, with Bank of the Pacific subsequently merging into Banner Bank. Each Pacific Financial share will be converted into a fixed exchange ratio of Banner common stock (specific ratio not stated in filing). The transaction is structured as a stock-for-stock merger. No price per share, premium, or break fee is disclosed. The merger requires shareholder votes at both companies and regulatory approvals. The filing includes a preliminary proxy statement/prospectus. Key watchpoints include shareholder approval timelines and regulatory clearance from banking regulators.

AZO.brief: AutoZone filed an 8-K announcing its Board authorized an additional $1.5 billion in share repurchases under its ongoing buyback program, bringing total authorizations to $42.2 billion since 1998. No price per share or specific premium is given, as this is an open-market authorization. The program is discretionary and will be funded from free cash flow while maintaining credit ratings. No board recommendation, advisor, or regulatory clock applies. Watch for execution pace and potential impact on EPS, though no risk-arb angle exists as this is not a tender offer.

PTCT.brief: PTC Therapeutics filed an 8-K announcing the pricing of a $500M 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2031 offering, with an underwriter option for an additional $50M. Concurrently, PTC will use ~$328.8M of net proceeds to repurchase $222M of its outstanding 1.5% Convertible Senior Notes due 2026 in privately negotiated transactions. Remaining proceeds go to general corporate purposes and potential additional repurchases. The notes are unregistered and convertible. The offering is not contingent on the repurchases. Watch for execution of the concurrent note repurchases and any follow-on actions to manage maturities.

DKS.brief: DICK'S Sporting Goods filed an S-4/A registration statement for an exchange offer to swap up to $381,932,000 of its 4.000% Senior Notes due 2029. The company is offering to exchange any and all outstanding notes issued September 11, 2025 for registered notes with substantially identical terms. The exchange is intended to satisfy registration rights obligations. There is no board recommendation, advisor, premium, or change in economic terms. The exchange is not conditioned on a minimum tender. The deal mechanics involve a like-for-like principal exchange with no cash consideration. No regulatory clock applies beyond SEC effectiveness. What to watch: execution risk is minimal; the arbitrage angle is absent as this is a registration rights exchange with no price dislocation.

EAT.brief: Brinker International, Inc. filed an 8-K with Item 8.01 Other Events to announce the redemption of all its outstanding 8.250% Senior Notes due July 15, 2030. The redemption is set for July 15, 2026, at a price equal to 104.125% of principal plus accrued interest. No tender offer or exchange is involved; the company is exercising its call option. The notice of redemption was issued on June 16, 2026, and the form 8-K explicitly states it does not constitute a notice of redemption. This is a straightforward debt retirement, not a special situation, but it fits the issuer tender/redemption category. No board recommendation, advisor, or regulatory timeline beyond the redemption date is provided. The event removes the note overhang and reduces future interest expense; investors should monitor the redemption settlement and any subsequent refinancing plans.

HLIT.brief: Harmonic Inc. filed an 8-K announcing the completion of the sale of its Video Business to Leone Media Inc. (d/b/a MediaKind) for $145 million in cash. The purchase price is subject to customary working capital, cash, indebtedness, and selling expense adjustments. The Asset Purchase Agreement, dated March 20, 2026, includes a three-year non-compete and reciprocal indemnification. Neven Haltmayer, SVP and GM of the Video Business, resigned upon closing. No board recommendation or advisor is named. Pro forma financials were omitted as the business was previously reported as discontinued operations. What to watch: integration execution by MediaKind and Harmonic's post-divestiture strategy; risk-arb is limited as the deal is closed.

MAC.brief: Macerich filed an 8-K on June 29, 2026, announcing the full exercise of the underwriters' 30-day option to purchase an additional 2,100,000 shares of common stock at $23.12325 per share, under an underwriting agreement dated June 15, 2026. The company entered into additional forward sale agreements with forward purchasers to borrow and sell the option shares. Closing occurred June 26, 2026. Proceeds depend on future physical settlement of the forward agreements, expected by June 16, 2027. The company may elect cash or net share settlement. This is a capital-raising equity forward transaction, not a special situation.

NEO.brief: NeoGenomics, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a civil settlement with the DOJ on behalf of OIG-HHS regarding an internal investigation into compliance of consulting agreements with federal healthcare laws. The settlement requires a payment of $9,813,260, which is below the previously accrued reserve of $11.2 million. The filing is a regulatory disclosure of a legal resolution, not a special situation such as an acquisition, divestiture, or activist campaign. The settlement does not involve a change in control, restructuring, or capital return.

GNL.brief: Global Net Lease, Inc. filed Amendment No. 1 to its S-4 registration statement on June 17, 2026, in connection with its proposed merger with Modiv Industrial, Inc. Under the terms disclosed, GNL will acquire Modiv in an all-stock transaction. Modiv stockholders will receive a fixed exchange ratio of GNL common shares per Modiv share, though specific ratios and implied values are not detailed in this filing. The boards of both companies have approved the transaction. GNL is using its S-4 to register the shares to be issued. The transaction requires Modiv stockholder approval and regulatory clearance; a special meeting is to be called. Risk-arb watchers should focus on stockholder sentiment and closing conditions.

BCO.brief: Brinks filed an 8-K disclosing two shareholder lawsuits challenging its pending acquisition of NCR Atleos. Under the February 26, 2026 Merger Agreement, a Brink's subsidiary will merge with NCR Atleos, which will then be merged into another subsidiary. The all-stock deal is subject to shareholder votes at special meetings on June 30, 2026. The complaints, filed in New York Supreme Court, allege negligent misrepresentation in the NCR Atleos proxy statement. Brink's took no position on the lawsuits. The combination would create a cash-management powerhouse. Watch for potential settlement or court ruling that could delay close, affecting risk-arb spread.

AVGO.brief: Broadcom Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing pricing terms and results of cash tender offers for its outstanding senior notes. On June 17, 2026, Broadcom announced it would purchase, up to a $2.5 billion aggregate cap, six series of notes: 4.926% Senior Notes due 2037, 4.900% due 2038, 5.050% due 2030, 5.200% due 2032, 5.150% due 2031, and 4.900% due 2032. Pricing was set per the Offer to Purchase dated June 11, 2026. No board recommendation, advisor, premium percentage, or specific price per note was disclosed. The tender is a liability-management transaction to reduce debt. Watch for completion timeline and potential upsize.

ECHO.brief: EchoStar Corp filed an 8-K reporting that subsidiary DISH DBS Corporation made delayed interest payments on three series of notes (5.25% secured notes due 2026, 5.75% secured notes due 2028, and 5.125% unsecured notes due 2029) within the 30-day grace period, avoiding an Event of Default. The payments were deferred to preserve liquidity pending receipt of $20.25 billion from the AT&T Transactions, which have received FCC and DOJ approvals but remain subject to final FCC order and other closing conditions. This filing reflects debt management and liquidity planning rather than a transformative event.

ENPH.brief: Enphase Energy filed an 8-K disclosing a Tax Credit Transfer Agreement to sell up to $150 million of Section 45X advanced manufacturing production tax credits to a leading financial institution for up to $139.5 million, payable in four installments through 2027. The agreement involves standard conditions precedent, covenants, indemnification, and termination provisions. This transaction monetizes tax credits generated from eligible component production in the US. As a non-deal special situation, it falls under 'Other' categories like tax credit sales. Watch for payment milestones and the company's ability to generate sufficient credits to fulfill the agreement.

TTMI.brief: TTM Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTMI) filed an 8-K on June 17, 2026, announcing definitive stock purchase agreements to acquire two privately-held European companies: Swiss Technology Group AG (Zurich) and ILFA GmbH (Hannover, Germany). Both transactions are for all-cash consideration, with no specific price per share, premium, or implied value disclosed. Regulatory approvals are required; the company expects to close subject to those conditions. The board recommends the acquisitions, but no advisor is named. The combined acquisitions would establish TTM's presence in Europe, adding PCB and materials capabilities in medical, aerospace/defense, and other markets. Investors should watch for regulatory clearance timing and potential integration risks; no break fee or deal mechanics details are provided.

HUBB.brief: Hubbell Incorporated filed an 8-K announcing completion of its acquisition of NSI Electrical Buyer, Inc. (NSI Industries) for $3.0 billion in cash. The purchase was funded via a $900 million unsecured term loan, $1.9 billion in senior notes, and commercial paper. The target provides electrical fittings and wire management products for industrial, infrastructure, and commercial markets. All issued and outstanding shares were acquired from seller NSI Buyer, LP. Terms include customary cash, debt, working capital, and expense adjustments. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or break fee stated. The deal closed on June 9, 2026, with no further regulatory hurdles; watch integration progress and debt servicing.

INCY.brief: Incyte filed an 8-K under Items 8.01 and 9.01 announcing the completion of its acquisition of Vega Therapeutics, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Star Therapeutics LLC. The deal closed on July 6, 2026, with terms not disclosed. The acquisition adds VGA039, an anti-Protein S monoclonal antibody in Phase 3 for von Willebrand disease, to Incyte's hematology pipeline. No price, premium, board recommendation, advisors, or breakup fee were stated. The filing confirms consummation, not a new announcement. Watch for Phase 3 data readouts and potential label expansion, as VGA039 could be first-to-market for VWD prophylaxis. No risk-arb spread since terms are undisclosed.

SIG.brief: Signet Jewelers filed an 8-K reporting an accelerated share repurchase (ASR) agreement with Goldman Sachs to repurchase $50 million of its common shares. The company made an upfront payment and expects an initial delivery of ~480,000 shares on June 8, 2026. Final settlement is based on VWAP during the calculation period, expected between June 12 and July 17, 2026, with potential adjustments. The ASR is part of Signet's 2017 Share Repurchase Program, leaving ~$355 million in remaining authorization. No board recommendation or advisor is named. This deal represents a capital return via share buyback. Watch for final settlement timing, any adjustments to share delivery, and overall repurchase activity under the remaining authorization.

VRRM.brief: Verra Mobility Corporation filed an 8-K reporting that its Board formed a Transformation Committee on June 5, 2026, to oversee a transformation initiative. The committee will support management's review of business and financial strategies, cost optimization, growth opportunities, capital allocation, portfolio composition, financing, and capital expenditure plans, and make recommendations to the Board. The committee comprises Raj Ratnakar (chair), Douglas Davis, and John Rexford. No specific terms, premium, or advisor are disclosed. This is an early-stage strategic review. Watch for further updates on potential divestitures, restructuring, or capital allocation changes; no immediate risk-arb angle.

AX.brief: Axos Financial, Inc. reported via Form 8-K that its subsidiary, Axos Nevada Holding, LLC, entered a definitive agreement to acquire Arc Technologies, Inc., a fintech platform for tech/growth companies. Terms (price, premium) are undisclosed; the deal is expected to close later in July 2026 and deemed not material to results/conditions. A press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1. No board recommendation or advisor named. The acquisition aims to accelerate Axos' digital strategy by adding cash management, capital markets, and AI capabilities for small businesses. Watch for regulatory clearance and integration updates given the quick close timeline.

EVTC.brief: EVERTEC filed an 8-K disclosing a cybersecurity incident where unauthorized access to client data occurred via a third-party support platform. The breach potentially exposed transaction records, payment card numbers, and customer names of financial institution clients in Puerto Rico. The company has contained the intrusion, notified law enforcement, and engaged external experts. No operational disruption has occurred. The investigation is ongoing, with full impact undetermined; expenses are expected but insurance coverage uncertain. This is a regulatory disclosure of an operational event, not a special situation—no deal terms or strategic action is involved. Risk-arb angle is not applicable.

SMCI.brief: Super Micro Computer, Inc. filed a 424B5 preliminary prospectus supplement for a $1.25B common stock offering (price to be determined; June 9, 2026 close $40.64). Concurrently, it is offering 75M depositary shares representing mandatory convertible preferred stock and plans a $2B ATM program. No board recommendation or advisor named. Proceeds will fund component purchases to fulfill ~$39B in AI server orders and for general corporate purposes. Closings are not conditioned on each other. Watch for pricing, overallotment option exercise, and impact from the concurrent financings on stock price.

CE.brief: New York Stock Exchange filed Form 25-NSE to delist the 4.777% Senior Notes Due 2026 guaranteed by Celanese Corp. The entire class of securities was called for redemption on June 25, 2026, with sufficient funds deposited and made available to holders. The delisting will be effective at the opening of business on July 6, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The filing is a routine administrative notice following full redemption; no structural or contest dynamics apply. The risk-arb angle is nil — all securities have been retired and paid.

JJSF.brief: J&J Snack Foods filed an 8-K regarding Amendment No. 2 to its credit agreement, extending the revolving facility maturity to 2031, increasing capacity by up to $200M (or EBITDA-based amount), and raising leverage ratio covenants. No acquisition, divestiture, or special situation event is announced; this is a routine credit facility amendment. The filing includes departure of a named officer (item 5.02), but no forced departure details are provided, and terms/advisor are absent. Watch for future acquisition use of the expanded facility.

WDC.brief: Western Digital Corp filed an 8-K Item 8.01 disclosing privately negotiated exchange agreements with institutional investors. The company will exchange 1,038,681 shares of Sandisk Corp common stock it holds for an equal-value number of shares of its own common stock, based on three-day volume-weighted average prices from June 16-18, 2026. The exchange closes June 22, 2026. This is an in-kind swap reducing Western Digital's Sandisk stake, not a conventional M&A or capital-return event; no premium, break fee, or board recommendation is cited. Watch for any subsequent 13D/13G filings from investors adjusting holdings post-closing.

LAZ.brief: Lazard, Inc. filed an 8-K to disclose its agreement to acquire all issued shares of Campbell Lutyens Holdings Limited, a private capital advisor. Total consideration is up to $660 million: $460 million initial (primarily in Lazard common stock at $46.50/share), $115 million deferred at two-year anniversary, and up to $85 million earn-out based on 2030 revenue targets. The transaction is expected to close with 100% ownership. Board supports the deal. Risk-arb focus: stock election mechanics, regulatory clearances, and earn-out achievability.

PB.brief: Prosperity Bancshares filed an 8-K announcing completion of its acquisition of Stellar Bancorp effective July 1, 2026. Each Stellar share was converted into 0.3803 Prosperity shares plus $11.36 cash, implying a total per-share consideration valued using a $71.44 reference price for Prosperity stock. Stellar stock options were cashed out based on the per-share merger consideration value. The merger was structured as a tax-free reorganization with Prosperity as the surviving entity, followed by a bank merger into Prosperity Bank. The deal closed with no disclosed regulatory hurdles; future updates may address integration milestones and accretion.

SKY.brief: Champion Homes, Inc. filed an 8-K on May 26, 2026, announcing its Q4 FY2026 earnings and a $50 million increase to its existing share repurchase program, refreshing the authorization to $150 million. The filing covers Items 2.02 and 8.01; no M&A, activist, or other special-situation trigger is present. The repurchase program increase is a discretionary capital-return action. The company's board approved the expansion; no advisor or timeline is stated. The purchases will occur in the open market or via other methods. Watch for the pace of buybacks and potential EPS accretion as the company executes the program.

ATEN.brief: A10 Networks, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing quarterly dividend approval by its Board. The dividend is $0.06 per share, payable June 1, 2026 to holders of record May 15, 2026. No stated premium, deal value, or advisor is provided. Future dividends are subject to Board review and potential adjustment. The filing is a capital-return event through a newly initiated quarterly dividend program. What to watch: sustainability of the dividend and any changes to the company's capital allocation strategy.

TECH.brief: Bio-Techne Corp filed an 8-K announcing entry into a definitive merger agreement with Merck KGaA and its wholly-owned subsidiary EMD Holdings NewCo, Inc. Under the agreement, Merger Sub will merge with and into Bio-Techne, with Bio-Techne surviving as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Parent. Shareholders will receive $73.00 per share in cash, valuing the equity at an implied enterprise value based on the cash consideration. The board has approved the merger, declared it advisable, and recommends shareholder approval. No premium percentage or break fee was stated. The transaction is subject to shareholder approval and customary closing conditions. Watch for shareholder vote timeline and potential competing bids.

CDW.brief: CDW Corp filed an 8-K disclosing a $1 billion increase to its existing share repurchase program, effective immediately. The increase is incremental to approximately $484 million remaining under the program as of March 31, 2026. Purchases may occur in open market or private transactions based on market conditions; no specific price, premium, or timeline is set. The board authorized the increase without naming an advisor. The program does not obligate CDW to repurchase any shares and may be modified or suspended. The filing is a routine capital return disclosure with no M&A or special-situation catalyst; watch for ongoing buyback execution.

RAL.brief: Ralliant Corp filed an 8-K on May 12, 2026, disclosing entry into an accelerated share repurchase (ASR) program to repurchase $100 million of its common stock under a pre-existing Board-authorized buyback. The repurchase price is based on the average daily Rule 10b-18 volume-weighted average price during the program term, with settlement expected by end of Q2 2026. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The ASR is a cash-settled structure reducing share count. Watch for final settlement shares repurchased and any impact on EPS; no arbitrage angle exists as this is an issuer capital return.

PTEN.brief: Patterson-UTI Energy filed an 8-K regarding a $500M offering of 6.050% Senior Notes due 2036 via an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, and Scotia Capital. Proceeds will redeem its 3.95% Senior Notes due 2028 (approx. $482.5M outstanding) plus general corporate purposes. The conditional redemption notice requires debt offering completion by June 4, 2026; close expected May 19, 2026. This is a refinancing transaction, not a return of capital to shareholders; thus categorized as Capital Returns with medium confidence as it primarily redeems existing debt.

EXE.brief: Expand Energy Corp filed Form 15 to terminate registration under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act for its Class A, B, and C Warrants, as of February 18, 2026. The filing indicates zero holders of record for each warrant class at certification, meeting the conditions for deregistration. The company, formerly Chesapeake Energy, is an Oklahoma-based oil and gas producer. The move suspends reporting obligations under Sections 13(a) and 15(d) for the warrants. No transaction terms, board recommendation, or advisor are mentioned. Watch for any remaining common stock reporting requirements and potential delisting implications.

NWE.brief: NorthWestern Energy Group filed a definitive proxy statement (DEFM14A) regarding its all-stock merger with Black Hills Corporation, announced August 18, 2025. Under the agreement, NorthWestern shareholders will receive 0.98 Black Hills common shares for each NorthWestern share held. The combined company, to be renamed (Newco), will list on NYSE. Both boards recommend the deal; no advisor named. Special shareholder meetings are set for April 2, 2026, held virtually. Merger sub will merge into NorthWestern, making it a Black Hills subsidiary. No break fee or regulatory timeline specified. Watch for shareholder votes and any regulatory hurdles; the 0.98 ratio may shift with Black Hills stock price.

AIG.brief: AIG filed an 8-K reporting Q1 2026 results and announcing an 11% increase in its quarterly cash dividend to $0.50 per share. The dividend hike is a capital-return event, not a routine earnings release. The board declared the increased dividend effective immediately. No advisor or recommendation was cited. The filing is a standard 8-K; the dividend increase is a direct return of capital to shareholders. What to watch: sustainability of payout ratio and potential for further shareholder distributions via buybacks.

EXPE.brief: Expedia Group filed an 8-K reporting Q1 2026 results and declaring a $0.48/share quarterly dividend ($0.48 annualized, payable June 18, 2026 to holders of record May 28, 2026). Additionally, the board authorized a $5 billion share repurchase program, complementing $700M in buybacks during Q1. The filing highlights strong operational performance (13% gross bookings growth, 15% revenue growth, 83% Adj. EBITDA increase). No advisor or premium is applicable, as this is a capital-return event. The mechanics involve a regular dividend and open-market repurchases. Watch for execution pace of the buyback and any impact on EPS.

RYAN.brief: Ryan Specialty Holdings filed an 8-K on April 30, 2026, reporting Q3 fiscal results and declaring a regular quarterly dividend of $0.13 per share on Class A common stock, payable May 26, 2026 to holders of record May 12, 2026. The dividend is a capital return event. The board approved this payment, with no special advisors named. The press release is furnished under Item 2.02. What to watch: future dividend patterns and payout sustainability.

FTV.brief: The New York Stock Exchange LLC filed a Form 25-NSE to delist Fortive Corp's 3.700% Notes due 2026 under Rule 12d2-2(a)(2). The securities were redeemed or paid at maturity on February 13, 2026, with trading suspended same day. Delisting becomes effective at the opening on February 24, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor was named. This is a routine notification of maturity, not a merger or take-private. The notes are fully collateralized by the issuer's obligation to pay. No overhang, ownership split, or regulatory clock applies. What to watch: confirm the full redemption price; risk-arb angle is negligible as this is a scheduled maturity event.

AON.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed Form 25-NSE to delist Aon plc's 2.875% Senior Notes due 2026 (SEC file 001-07933). The notes were called for redemption/maturity on February 14, 2026, with funds deposited and made available to holders. Trading was suspended on February 17, 2026, and removal from listing is effective March 2, 2026. No board recommendation, advisor, or contest is involved. This is a routine debt-security delisting per Rule 12d2-2(a)(1). Risk-arb angle: no equity event; watch for future debt issuances by Aon.

SGI.brief: Somnigroup International Inc. (formerly Tempur Sealy) filed Amendment No. 1 to its S-4 registration statement on July 8, 2026, in connection with its proposed merger with Leggett & Platt, Incorporated. The merger agreement was entered into on April 13, 2026. Under the terms, Leggett & Platt shareholders will receive a combination of cash and Somnigroup stock (consideration structure not fully specified in this excerpt). The board of Leggett & Platt recommends shareholders vote for the merger; Cleary Gottlieb and Latham & Watkins are advisors. The merger requires regulatory approval and shareholder votes. The filing is a proxy statement/prospectus; the transaction is subject to SEC effectiveness and customary closing conditions. What to watch: shareholder vote timing and antitrust review risk.

GVA.brief: Granite Construction closed a private offering of $600M 6.375% senior notes due 2034, generating ~$590M net proceeds. The proceeds, plus cash on hand and capped call payments, will redeem all outstanding 3.75% convertible notes due 2028, repay credit facility borrowings, and for general corporate purposes. The notes are senior unsecured and guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries that are borrowers under the credit facility. The filing primarily describes a refinancing and debt restructuring rather than a pure capital return, but the redemption of convertible notes with cash qualifies as a capital return to prior noteholders. Watch for interest rate environment shifts and credit rating impact.

GPN.brief: Global Payments Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing an accelerated share repurchase (ASR) program to repurchase $500 million of its common stock, part of a previously announced board-approved repurchase plan. Approximately 5.74 million shares will be received on May 8, 2026, with final settlement expected by June 30, 2026. The total shares repurchased will be based on the average daily VWAP during the repurchase period, less a discount and subject to adjustments. This is a capital return event via an ASR, not a tender offer. Watch for the final share count and impact on EPS.

LNC.brief: Lincoln National Corporation filed an S-4 registration statement on February 20, 2026, for an exchange offer to swap up to $500 million of outstanding 2.330% Senior Notes due 2030 (issued May 15, 2025) for registered notes with identical terms. The exchange is being made to satisfy registration rights; no new capital is raised. The board supports the transaction; Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz serves as legal counsel. Mechanics: holders exchange existing notes (CUSIP 534187 BM0) for registered notes (CUSIP 534187 BY4) on a like-for-like basis. There is no premium, break fee, or regulatory clock beyond SEC effectiveness. The transaction is purely a registration cure, not a tender or consent solicitation—risk-arb is inapplicable; focus on SEC effectiveness timing and any holdout dynamics.

MS.brief: Morgan Stanley filed an 8-K to announce a quarterly common stock dividend increase to $1.15 per share from $1.00, a 15% rise. The dividend applies to the common stock and will commence with the declaration expected in the quarter ending September 30, 2026. The board authorized the increase, reflecting strong capital position. Terms include per-share amount only; no premium, advisors, or structural conditions. This is a routine capital return action not linked to any other event. Watch for sustained earnings coverage and payout ratio evolution.

ROCK.brief: Gibraltar Industries (ROCK) filed an 8-K reporting the sale of its Renewables racking and foundations business to Unirac for $5 million in cash, subject to customary post-closing adjustments. This sale completes the divestiture of the Renewables business, following the earlier sale of the electrical balance-of-systems portion on February 20, 2026. The Renewables business was classified as held for sale and reported as discontinued operations from June 30, 2025. The company is simplifying its asset portfolio, focusing on building products and structures end markets. The transaction is valued at $5 million, with no disclosed premium or advisor. Watch for completion of post-closing adjustments and potential proceeds use.

KDP.brief: Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. filed an 8-K on June 23, 2026, disclosing that Coffee Operating Unit head Rafa Oliveira will depart at end of July 2026 for an external CEO role. CEO Tim Cofer will temporarily oversee the coffee business while the Board searches for a CEO of Global Coffee Co., a standalone entity expected from the previously-announced separation of KDP's coffee and beverage businesses. The filing also reaffirms 2026 guidance. No deal terms were provided. This event updates the progress of a planned spin-off, announced earlier, which is the core special situation. The filing does not trigger a new deal category but supports the existing spin-off classification. Watch for further separation details and CEO appointment timeline.

MLM.brief: Martin Marietta Materials Inc. files Form 8-K disclosing amendments to its $800M revolver and a new $1.5B term loan facility to fund cash consideration for its previously announced acquisition of Lhoist North America, Inc. The credit agreements include a temporary leverage covenant step-up to 4.75x post-closing, stepping down to 3.75x. The term loan matures in three years with SOFR- or base-rate-based pricing. No per-share price, premium, or advisor named. Watch for regulatory clearances and closing conditions; risk-arb focuses on leverage and financing execution.

AMGN.brief: Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed Form 25-NSE to delist Amgen Inc.'s 2.000% Senior Notes due 2026 under Rule 12d2-2(a)(2). The delisting is effective as of February 24, 2026, and reflects the securities' maturity. No premium, stock consideration, or board involvement applies. This is a routine administrative removal of matured notes, not a merger or tender. The filing has no regulatory clock or risk-arb implications; the notes will cease trading on Nasdaq. What to watch: any residual claims or conversion rights tied to the matured notes.

EXPD.brief: Expeditors International filed an 8-K on May 5, 2026, announcing a semi-annual cash dividend of $0.81 per share declared May 4, 2026, payable June 15, 2026 to holders of record June 1, 2026. This represents a 5% increase from prior dividends. The company also highlighted a new $3 billion share repurchase program authorized in February 2026 and cumulative returns of nearly $2 billion to shareholders since 2024. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The filing is a routine dividend declaration and ongoing buyback program disclosure. What to watch: no risk-arb angle; this is a steady capital return policy.

UTL.brief: Unitil Corp filed an 8-K reporting Amendment No. 4 to its Purchase and Sale Agreement with Aquarion Water Authority, changing the acquisition scope from three subsidiaries (AWC-MA, AWC-NH, Abenaki) to only AWC-NH and Abenaki, effectively narrowing the deal. The prior amendments extended the termination date to June 30, 2026. No financial terms, price/share, premium, or board recommendation were disclosed in this excerpt. The filing includes an Operating and Transition Services Agreement. Watch for regulatory approvals and any further adjustments as the revised transaction proceeds toward close.

CWT.brief: California Water Service Group filed an 8-K under Item 8.01 to announce its board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.3350 per common share, payable May 22, 2026, to holders of record May 11, 2026. This marks the 325th consecutive quarterly dividend. No special-situation event such as an acquisition, divestiture, activist campaign, strategic review, tender offer, going-private, capital return, spin-off, rights offering, restructuring, liquidation, delisting, issuer tender, deal termination, SPAC, or management change is present. The filing is a routine dividend declaration, not a special situation.

LFST.brief: LifeStance Health Group filed an 8-K reporting a secondary offering of 35 million shares by selling stockholders, with the issuer repurchasing 6 million shares from the underwriter at the same price. The company received no proceeds; the closing occurred on May 12, 2026. The filing is an ordinary equity offering disclosure under Item 8.01, not a special situation. No activist, strategic review, or transformative event is present. The filing is a routine current report.

JOE.brief: The St. Joe Company filed an 8-K disclosing a $150.8 million increase in its share repurchase authorization, bringing total capacity to $200.0 million under the existing Stock Repurchase Program with no expiration date. The company had $49.2 million remaining prior to the expansion. This is an issuer-initiated capital return via open-market buybacks, not a tender offer. There is no stated price, premium, or timeline. The board authorized the additional repurchase capacity as a discretionary use of corporate cash. Investors should watch actual repurchase execution pace and any impact on diluted share count or earnings per share.

TTD.brief: Trade Desk, Inc. disclosed in an 8-K filed 2026-03-25 that it fell out of compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rules 5605(c)(2)(A) and 5605(d)(2)(A) after the resignations of directors Alexander Kayyal (3/19) and Kathryn Falberg (3/23). The audit and compensation committees lost minimum independent director counts. Nasdaq granted a cure period through 9/21/2026. The board appointed Andrew Vollero as Class II director and to the audit committee effective 4/3/2026, partially addressing the vacancies. No shareholder vote, premium, or price is involved. Watch for appointment of additional independent directors to regain compliance by the deadline; delisting risk remains if uncured.

INTU.brief: Intuit Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a restructuring plan to simplify its organizational structure, reducing its workforce by ~17% and considering site closures. The company expects $300-$340 million in charges, primarily for severance and benefits, mostly in Q4 fiscal 2026 ending July 31, 2026, with actions substantially completed by Q1 fiscal 2027 ending October 31, 2026. The board approved a cash dividend. This is a cost-cutting restructuring, not a sale or acquisition. Watch for execution risk and further charges.

URBN.brief: This 8-K Item 8.01 filing reports Urban Outfitters, Inc.'s earnings release for the quarter ended April 30, 2026, disclosing record net sales of $1.48 billion (up 11.4%) and net income of $115.7 million ($1.30 EPS). No strategic event or transaction is announced; it is a routine earnings disclosure without any special-situation elements such as M&A, activism, or restructuring. The filing is purely informational and does not trigger corporate action.

EFC.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed a Form 25-NSE to delist Ellington Financial Inc.'s 6.750% Series A Fixed-to-Floating Rate Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock. The entire class was called for redemption on February 27, 2026, with funds sufficient for payment deposited and made available to holders. Trading was suspended as of that date, and delisting becomes effective at the opening of business on March 10, 2026, per Rule 12d2-2(a)(1). No board recommendation or advisor was noted. This is a routine mandatory delisting following a full redemption; the risk-arb angle is moot as the security is being retired at par.

VNOM.brief: Viper Energy filed a prospectus supplement to its automatic shelf registration statement on Form S-3 for the sale of up to 3,691,796 shares of Class A common stock by a selling stockholder. The filing includes an opinion of Latham & Watkins LLP on the legality of the securities. No terms such as price per share or premium are disclosed; the registrant is the issuer facilitating a secondary sale. This is a routine shelf takedown, not a transformative special situation. The event is a capital markets transaction with no advisory, board recommendation, or structural complexity beyond equity distribution. Watch for selling shareholder identity and potential market overhang.

GATX.brief: GATX Corporation filed an 8-K on July 1, 2026, disclosing the exercise of the first call option under a pre-existing Call Option Agreement to acquire an additional interest in GABX Leasing Holding LLC (Blocker), increasing its indirect interest in the GABX Leasing LLC joint venture from 30% to approximately 33.535%. The remaining ~66.465% is held by Brookfield Infrastructure partners. Concurrently, the Blocker LLC agreement was amended and restated, granting GATX joint approval rights over fundamental actions and admitting it as a member while Brookfield remains Managing Member. The Call Option Agreement was previously filed on January 5, 2026. This is a contractual step-up, not a transformative event—no price, premium, or tender terms disclosed. Watch for subsequent call exercises per the option agreement schedule.

T.brief: NYSE filed Form 25-NSE to delist AT&T Inc.'s 0.250% Global Notes due 2026, citing Rule 12d2-2(a)(2) as the securities were redeemed at maturity on March 4, 2026. The removal from listing is effective March 16, 2026, with trading suspended from March 4. As a bond redemption, there is no premium, board recommendation, or advisor. This is a routine delisting of a maturing debt security, involving no equity risk or activist event. What to watch: no further trading or settlement impact; focus shifts to AT&T's overall debt maturity profile.

VICI.brief: VICI Properties filed an S-4/A registering shares to be issued in connection with its acquisition of Golden Entertainment, Inc. VICI will issue VICI common stock to holders of Golden common stock as merger consideration. The board of Golden has recommended the transaction; no advisor named in the excerpt. The merger will be effected under Minnesota law; VICI common stock is to be listed on NYSE. The transaction is subject to regulatory approval and Golden stockholder vote. What to watch: execution risk from regulatory clearance and stockholder approval; risk-arb spread will depend on VICI share price volatility.

PAYC.brief: Paycom Software filed an 8-K announcing a $0.375/share quarterly cash dividend and a new $2.0 billion stock repurchase plan with no expiration date. The dividend will be paid June 8, 2026 to holders of record May 26, 2026. Repurchases may be executed via open-market, privately negotiated, or Rule 10b5-1 programs at the board's discretion. No break fee or premium applies; this is a pure capital-return initiative. The company may use cash or its credit facility to fund repurchases. Watch for execution pace and any suspension triggers based on market conditions; no risk-arb angle as there is no M&A.

CL.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed a Form 25-NSE to remove from listing and registration the entire class of Colgate-Palmolive Co's 0.500% Notes due 2026, effective at the opening on March 17, 2026. The action follows the redemption or maturity of the notes on March 6, 2026, as permitted under SEC Rule 12d2-2(a)(2). Trading of the notes was suspended on March 6, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor was named. This is a routine delisting for matured debt; no premium or shareholder vote applies. The filing confirms the final extinguishment of the security. Watch for any residual claims or conversion terms; risk-arb implications are nil.

MZTI.brief: The Marzetti Company filed an 8-K reporting the closing of a $200 million term loan to partially fund its $400 million acquisition of Bachan's, Inc., a Japanese barbecue sauce brand, with the balance from cash on hand. The term loan, drawn on April 29, 2026, matures April 29, 2031, with a springing maturity date of March 6, 2029 under certain conditions; quarterly principal payments of $2.5 million begin after the first full calendar quarter. The acquisition closed on the same date. Watch for integration updates and margin impact; no arb angle as deal is cash and closed.

SLM.brief: SLM Corp filed a prospectus supplement (424B5) for a registered offering of $500M aggregate principal amount of 6.495% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Senior Notes due 2032. The notes bear initial fixed interest at 6.495% through May 15, 2031, then float at Compounded SOFR plus 271 bps. Price to public is 100%, underwriting discount 1%, net proceeds $495M. The notes are unsecured senior obligations, unlisted, and structurally subordinated to subsidiary liabilities. Joint book-running managers are J.P. Morgan and Barclays. This is a plain-vanilla debt issuance, not a special situation.

EXLS.brief: ExlService Holdings, through its indirect subsidiary Clairvoyant AI, entered a securities purchase agreement to acquire 100% of iMerit for $170M upfront cash (subject to adjustments) plus up to $140M in cash incentives/earnouts over two years. The transaction is expected to close Q3 2026, pending antitrust clearance and customary conditions. The acquirer plans to fund with cash on hand and credit facility. Board approval is implied; no advisor named. Watch for regulatory timing and earnout milestone definitions as risk-arb drivers.

HUBG.brief: Hub Group, Inc. disclosed receipt of a Nasdaq Staff Deficiency Notice for failing to timely file its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, in violation of Nasdaq Listing Rule 5250(c)(1). The company is already on a 180-day exception period until September 14, 2026, to file its delinquent Form 10-K for FY2025. Hub Group must submit an updated compliance plan by June 3, 2026. The delisting notice has no immediate effect on trading. Watch for the submission of the updated plan and progress on filing both periodic reports within the exception window.

GNW.brief: Genworth Financial filed a definitive proxy statement (DEFC14A) for its 2026 annual meeting, addressing a contested solicitation. No specific terms were provided regarding stake, price, or premium. The board's recommendation is anticipated but not detailed in the excerpt. The filing includes disclosures on capital generation from Enact ($98 million dividends, $309 million share repurchases) and a $350 million share repurchase program, with $856 million repurchased since May 2022. Mechanics involve a shareholder vote on director elections and other proposals. Regulatory clock aligns with typical proxy timeline. What to watch: outcome of contested election and any activist influence on capital allocation.

MBC.brief: MasterBrand, Inc. filed an 8-K to report the closing of its acquisition of American Woodmark Corporation via a merger. At closing, each American Woodmark share was exchanged for 5.150 shares of MasterBrand common stock (stock consideration). No cash or premium percentage was explicitly stated. Equity awards were converted based on the same exchange ratio. The board of each company approved the deal; no advisors named. The merger was effective May 28, 2026, and MasterBrand is the surviving public company. The market should monitor post-close integration and any stock price adjustments reflecting the exchange ratio.

BMY.brief: Bristol-Myers Squibb filed Form 15 to terminate the registration of its $2 Convertible Preferred Stock and 43 other classes of debt securities under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act, effective March 27, 2026. The filing states there are zero holders of record for the affected securities, meeting the threshold to suspend reporting obligations. No board recommendation, advisor, or financial terms were disclosed. This deregistration reduces ongoing SEC compliance costs but does not affect the company's common stock or contingent value rights. The move is procedural following prior redemptions or conversions. Watch for any remaining litigation or contingent value right triggers.

JBSS.brief: John B. Sanfilippo & Son, Inc. (JBSS) filed an 8-K announcing a special cash dividend of $1.05 per share and a regular annual cash dividend of $0.95 per share on both Common and Class A Common stock. The aggregate payment will return approximately $23.6 million to stockholders. Dividends are payable September 9, 2026, to holders of record August 17, 2026. The special dividend is a one-time capital return event. The annual dividend represents a $0.05 increase year-over-year. The filing does not mention any advisor or board recommendation beyond the dividend declaration. No structural complexities or regulatory clock are noted. What to watch: future capital allocation policies and whether special dividends become recurring.

BTSG.brief: BrightSpring Health Services, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting an underwriting agreement dated June 3, 2026 for a secondary offering of 14,999,771 shares of common stock at $58.75 per share by selling stockholders, including KKR Phoenix Aggregator L.P. and management stockholders. The company did not receive proceeds except from stock option exercises, and repurchased 1,026,465 shares from the underwriter. The offering was made under an existing Form S-3ASR. While the share repurchase is a capital return element, the filing primarily discloses a secondary sale by existing holders, not a transformative special situation. Watch for any further KKR stake reduction or insider selling; no risk-arb angle applicable.

DCOM.brief: Dime Community Bancshares voluntarily filed Form 25 to delist its common stock, Series A preferred stock, and 9.000% subordinated notes from Nasdaq, effective April 6, 2026. The issuer certified compliance with Exchange Act Rule 12d2-2(c) for voluntary withdrawal. No consideration, premium, or shareholder vote was required. The delisting likely precedes a going-private transaction, merger, or capital restructuring. Watch for a subsequent Schedule 13E-3 or merger announcement detailing a buyout or consolidation. Risk-arb focus: whether a public-to-private premium emerges.

INSW.brief: International Seaways, Inc. filed an 8-K on May 11, 2026, disclosing entry into an Equity Distribution Agreement to sell up to $200 million of its common stock in at-the-market offerings through agents BTIG, B. Riley, Clarksons, and Fearnleys. Each agent receives up to 3% commission. No shares have been sold yet. This ATM program is a capital-raising mechanism rather than a definitive capital return event. As an issuer shelf takedown with no immediate transaction, it does not fit standard special-situations categories. The filing is routine and not a special situation.

RCUS.brief: Arcus Biosciences filed an 8-K under Item 8.01 to disclose the discontinuation of the Phase 3 STAR-121 study due to futility (domvanalimab plus zimberelimab and chemotherapy), as recommended by the IDMC; and that Gilead will not make an option continuation payment, ending its option rights to additional early-stage programs (CCR6, CD89, CD40L) after July 14, 2026. Gilead retains limited options to AB801, AB598, AB102, and a TNF small-molecule inhibitor. Arcus retains full rights to casdatifan except those licensed to Taiho. No financial terms, deal mechanics, or board recommendation were provided. Watch for any restructuring of the Gilead collaboration or potential impact on Arcus's pipeline valuation.

NXPI.brief: NXP Semiconductors N.V. filed an 8-K announcing that its subsidiary NXP B.V., along with NXP USA Inc. and NXP Funding LLC, redeemed $750 million in aggregate principal of its 3.875% senior notes due June 2026. The redemption was conducted per the indenture terms, funded by the issuer. The press release highlights capital allocation commitment alongside share repurchases and dividends. No premium, price per share, or board recommendation is specified as this is a debt redemption, not equity. Watch for potential impacts on leverage ratios and future capital allocation updates.

NTST.brief: NETSTREIT Corp. filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement establishing a new $400M ATM equity offering program, replacing a prior $300M program. The company enters into a sales agreement with multiple agents and forward sellers, allowing for sales of common stock from time to time. As of the filing, $256.1M in shares have been sold under the prior program, and 12.8M shares remain unsettled under forward sale agreements maturing September 2026 through March 2027. This is a routine capital-raising transaction, not a special situation.

STT.brief: State Street Corporation filed a preliminary prospectus supplement (424B5) for an underwritten public offering of fixed-to-floating rate senior notes due 2032 and 2037. The aggregate principal amounts, fixed rates, floating spreads, and final terms are to be determined. The notes are unsecured, rank equally with other senior unsecured debt, are not FDIC-insured, and are not listed on any exchange. Joint book-running managers are Morgan Stanley, Deutsche Bank Securities, Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, and UBS Investment Bank. This is a routine debt capital markets transaction, not a special situation. Proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes. No special-situation dynamics apply.

BRC.brief: Brady Corp (BRC) signed a definitive equity purchase agreement to acquire Honeywell International’s Productivity Solutions & Services business for $1.4 billion in cash. The transaction is expected to close in H2 2026. Financing will come from new debt and cash on hand; BMO Capital Markets committed up to $1.8 billion in bridge facilities (Tranche A $1B, Tranche B $800M). The acquisition is not financing-conditioned. Regulatory clearance under HSR is required. A pre-closing internal reorganization by the seller is a condition. Watch for antitrust review timing and integration risk; the all-cash deal reduces execution uncertainty.

CALX.brief: Calix filed an 8-K reporting that its Board increased the existing stock repurchase authorization by an additional $100 million, bringing total authorization to $525 million. The remaining authorization as of March 28, 2026, was $63.4 million. Repurchases may be made via open market or private transactions at the company's discretion, with no obligation to acquire a specific amount. The program can be suspended anytime. Watch for actual buyback execution pace relative to disclosed availability; no advisor mentioned.

DFIN.brief: Donnelley Financial Solutions filed an 8-K reporting that its Board authorized a new $150 million share repurchase program, replacing a prior program with ~$15 million remaining. Repurchases may occur on the open market or in private transactions through December 31, 2027, and may be executed under a Rule 10b5-1 plan. No price/share, premium, or advisor is stated. The repurchase is an ordinary capital return event, not a tender offer. Watch for the pace of buybacks and possible suspension if market conditions change.

ONTO.brief: Onto Innovation Inc. filed an 8-K announcing plans for a private offering of $1.1B aggregate principal amount of convertible senior notes due 2031, under Rule 144A. The proceeds will be used for share repurchases and capped call transactions. No specific price per share, premium, or board recommendation was disclosed. The offering is subject to market conditions. The mechanics include a convertible issuance alongside hedging via capped calls to reduce dilution. Watch: pricing terms, conversion premium, and overall capital return impact to equity value.

DDOG.brief: Datadog filed an 8-K reporting shareholder approval and completion of a redomiciliation from Delaware to Nevada via a plan of conversion, effective April 21, 2026. The reorganization did not change business, management, assets, or stock terms. No price, premium, or deal value is involved. New indemnification agreements were entered with officers and directors. This is a jurisdictional reincorporation, not a special-situation transaction, so the filing is classified as Other.

NHC.brief: National Healthcare Corp. (NHC) filed an 8-K reporting completion of its $560 million cash acquisition of 35 skilled nursing and independent living facilities from National Health Investors (NHI) on July 1, 2026. The purchase was funded by borrowings under a credit facility from Bank of America and cash on hand. NHC previously leased these properties. The credit agreement was amended to increase the revolver from $50M to $75M. No premium percentage, board recommendation, or advisor was disclosed. The transaction eliminates the master lease structure, converting NHC from tenant to owner-operator. Watch for integration execution and potential deleveraging actions.

NOW.brief: ServiceNow Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its entry into a $4 billion unsecured term loan credit agreement on April 17, 2026, to finance a portion of the cash consideration for its acquisition of Armis Security Ltd. The term loan matures on October 16, 2026, with interest at alternate base rate or term SOFR plus a margin based on credit ratings, and includes customary covenants and a potential six-month extension at lender discretion. JPMorgan Chase acted as administrative agent. The acquisition terms (price, premium, target advisors) and board recommendation were not disclosed. Watch for regulatory clearance and financing risk given short maturity.

CATY.brief: CATHAY GENERAL BANCORP filed an 8-K on April 23, 2026, announcing a new $150 million share repurchase program adopted by its board. The program allows open-market or private repurchases at management's discretion, potentially via a Rule 10b5-1 plan, with no fixed expiration. With ~67 million shares outstanding, the authorization represents ~$2.24/share. The board may suspend or modify the program at any time. What to watch: actual execution pace and any impact on capital ratios or EPS; risk-arb: none, as no M&A catalyst is present.

FFBC.brief: First Financial Bancorp filed an 8-K announcing a definitive merger agreement to acquire Finward Bancorp (seller) via stock-for-stock merger. Terms: each Finward share converts into 1.35 shares of First Financial common stock. The boards of both companies unanimously approved. Closing expected in Q4 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and Finward shareholder vote. Structure involves Finward merging into First Financial, with its bank subsidiary merging into First Financial Bank. Watch for regulatory timeline and shareholder approval risks; no premium percentage or break fee disclosed in filing.

HAFC.brief: Hanmi Financial Corp. filed an 8-K on April 23, 2026, announcing a $0.28 per share quarterly cash dividend declared by its Board of Directors, payable May 20, 2026, to holders of record May 4, 2026. The dividend is part of a capital return program; the press release also references a share repurchase program. No offer, tender, or structural change is involved; the filing is a routine dividend declaration with a note on buybacks. The action returns capital to shareholders without altering the corporate structure. Watch for any changes in payout policy or repurchase activity as signals.

PHM.brief: PulteGroup filed an 8-K disclosing Q1 2026 earnings and a $1.5 billion increase in its existing share repurchase program, effective April 22, 2026. The company reported net income of $347 million ($1.79 per share) and had already repurchased $308 million of common shares in the quarter. The board approved the authorization increase, but no specific price, premium, or expiration date was provided. The mechanics are a standard open-market buyback, which reduces share count and supports EPS. Watch for future buyback execution pace and any leverage impact; risk-arb is not applicable as this is purely a capital allocation event.

TMUS.brief: T-Mobile US filed an 8-K announcing its board increased the 2026 Shareholder Return Program by $3.6 billion, raising the total authorization from $14.6 billion to $18.2 billion through December 31, 2026. The program includes share repurchases and cash dividends; utilization depends on market conditions. The Q1 2026 dividend of $1.02/share was paid March 12, and Q2 2026 dividend of $1.02/share was declared March 19. No advisor or board recommendation was disclosed. The increase signals strong cash generation and shareholder commitment; watch actual repurchase pace and dividend policy for payout sustainability.

WABC.brief: Westamerica Bancorporation filed an 8-K announcing a board-approved increase in its stock repurchase plan authorization by 2,000,000 shares, bringing total remaining authorization to 2,785,023 shares (11.8% of shares outstanding as of March 31, 2026). Repurchases may occur on the open market or in privately negotiated transactions through December 31, 2026. Chair/CEO David Payne cited financial strength and capital-management goals. No price or premium terms are stated. The program is accretive to EPS but execution depends on market conditions. Watch the pace of buybacks relative to authorization as a signal of management's capital-return appetite.

JEF.brief: Jefferies Financial Group Inc. filed an 8-K announcing the pricing of a public offering of $1.1 billion aggregate principal amount of 5.125% Senior Notes due 2031, with an effective yield of 5.304% and maturity on April 28, 2031. The offering is expected to settle on April 28, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. Net proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes. Jefferies LLC acted as sole global coordinator and joint book-runner. This is a routine debt capital markets transaction and does not constitute a special situation event; therefore, no deal terms are applicable.

UHT.brief: Universal Health Realty Income Trust filed an 8-K on April 21, 2026, to report entering into a First Amendment to its Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement. The amendment adds a $50 million incremental term loan facility, adjusts the minimum tangible net worth requirement to $100 million, and removes the 0.10% Term SOFR Adjustment. A new subsidiary was added as a guarantor. The term loan matures on September 30, 2028, with interest based on SOFR or Base Rate plus a leverage-based margin. This is a routine debt financing modification, not a special situation. Watch for ongoing leverage ratio compliance and any future capital structure changes.

FBK.brief: FB Financial Corp filed an 8-K announcing its board renewed a stock repurchase plan authorizing up to $175 million of common stock repurchases, running until June 30, 2027, replacing a prior authorization. Repurchases may be executed via open market or private transactions under Rule 10b-18, with timing and amount subject to market conditions, regulatory constraints, and alternative capital uses. No specific price, premium, or advisor was disclosed. The plan reflects disciplined capital management and can be suspended anytime. Watch for execution pace and potential buyback impact on share price given the open-ended mechanics.

GILD.brief: Gilead Sciences filed an 8-K announcing completion of its acquisition of Arcellx, Inc. via a tender offer and merger. The consideration was $115.00 per share in cash plus one CVR (earn-out of $5.00 per CVR payable in 2030 if Arcellx's anito-cel product cumulative worldwide sales exceed $6.0B by December 31, 2029). The tender offer expired on April 27, 2026, with the merger effective April 28, 2026. No board recommendation or advisors are noted. The CVR includes a risk-arb angle as payout depends on commercial milestones; watch for future sales disclosures.

UMBF.brief: UMB Financial Corp filed an 8-K on April 28, 2026, announcing a $0.43 quarterly common dividend and a Series B preferred dividend of $193.75 per share ($0.484375 per depositary share). The board also authorized repurchase of up to two million common shares through the board meeting following the 2027 annual meeting. No price, premium, or advisor details are provided. These capital return actions are routine shareholder distributions. What to watch: actual share repurchase pace and any future capital management updates.

EIG.brief: Employers Holdings, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting Q1 2026 results, declaring a regular quarterly dividend of $0.34 per share payable May 27, 2026 to holders of record May 13, 2026, and authorizing a new $125 million share repurchase program (2026 Program) effective May 4, 2026 through December 31, 2027, replacing a fully utilized prior program. Repurchases may occur in open market or private transactions under Rules 10b5-1 and 10b-18. The dividend increase and buyback authorization signal a capital return to shareholders. Watch execution pace and any future program extensions.

STBA.brief: S&T Bancorp filed an 8-K to announce its board approved a $0.37 per share quarterly cash dividend, a $0.01 increase (2.78%) from the prior quarter and $0.03 (8.82%) from the year-ago period. The dividend yields 3.33% based on the April 28 closing price of $44.43. Payable May 28, 2026, to holders of record on May 14, 2026. The filing is a routine dividend increase, not a special situation involving a merger, tender offer, or restructuring. Watch for continued dividend growth as a sign of capital management discipline.

BDC.brief: Belden Inc. filed an 8-K to report the completion of its acquisition of Vistance Networks’ RUCKUS reporting segment (the "RUCKUS Acquisition") on July 1, 2026, pursuant to a Purchase Agreement dated April 29, 2026. To fund the transaction, Belden entered into a $1,850 million senior secured term loan credit facility maturing July 1, 2033, bearing interest at term SOFR + 2.25% or base rate + 1.25% p.a., with customary covenants. No per-share price, premium, or valuation details were disclosed. The Transaction is closed. What to watch: post-acquisition integration and debt-service metrics.

BLDR.brief: Builders FirstSource filed an 8-K reporting Q1 2026 results (net sales $3.3B, down 10.1%; net loss $47.4M) and announced a $500M share repurchase authorization. The buyback is a capital-return event, not a formal tender offer; the board authorized it without stated expiration. No price per share, premium, or advisor was specified. The program will be funded from operations, allowing open-market purchases at management's discretion. Watch for actual repurchase cadence and potential EPS accretion; the risk-arb angle is limited as this is an open-market program, not a tender.

ILMN.brief: Illumina filed an 8-K reporting Q1 2026 earnings (revenue $1.09B, GAAP EPS $0.87) and disclosed a new $1.5B share repurchase program authorized April 28, 2026, supplementing an August 2024 program with ~$314M remaining. The buyback signals management's confidence in cash flow and commitment to returning capital to shareholders. No specific price, premium, expiration, or advisor is stated. The program can be executed through open-market purchases or other means. Watch for pace of repurchase and potential EPS accretion; risk-arb angle is minimal as this is not a tender but a discretionary buyback authorization.

KAI.brief: Kadant Inc. filed an 8-K announcing its subsidiary Kadant Holdings GmbH completed the acquisition of voestalpine BÜHLER Profil GmbH & Co KG and voestalpine BÜHLER Profil VerwaltungsGmbH (now renamed Kadant Profil) for approximately €157.0 million in cash, subject to customary adjustments. The acquisition was primarily financed via borrowings under Kadant's revolving credit facility. Kadant Profil will be integrated into Kadant's Industrial Processing reporting segment. No board recommendation or advisor was disclosed. The purchase price implies a straightforward cash deal with no premium stated. The 8-K does not provide a timeline for purchase accounting or synergies. Watch for future earnings integration updates; no risk-arb angle as deal is closed.

MARA.brief: MARA Holdings, Inc. (MARA) filed an 8-K reporting that its subsidiary, Volt Texas, LLC, acquired all membership interests of MAT 1177 LLC from HIF USA LLC on July 2, 2026. The transaction closed on signing. The target holds land and a letter agreement for 2,000 MW of power capacity in Texas for a digital infrastructure campus. The aggregate purchase price is up to $600 million, structured as milestone payments tied to regulatory approvals, site acquisition, power authorization, and a lease execution. Seller retains a minority interest upon certain milestones. No formal advisor or recommendation was noted. What to watch: execution risk on achieving development milestones and partnership with Starwood Digital Ventures.

PRGO.brief: Perrigo Company plc filed an 8-K announcing the completion of the sale of its Dermacosmetics Business to an affiliate of Karo Healthcare AB, managed by KKR. The transaction closed on April 30, 2026, with a cash payment of €305.6 million, including net working capital adjustments, and up to €27.0 million in contingent consideration over three years. The board recommended the sale, though no specific advisors were named. The deal was executed via a Master Sale and Purchase Agreement with Kairos Bidco AB. Watch for further updates on the contingent earn-out and potential use of proceeds by Perrigo.

SNDR.brief: Schneider National filed an 8-K announcing a quarterly cash dividend of $0.10 per share on Class A and B common stock, approved by its Board on April 29, 2026. The dividend is payable to holders of record as of June 12, 2026, and expected to be paid on July 10, 2026. This is a routine capital return event, not a special situation. No premium, price per share, or deal structure is involved. The filing is a standard dividend declaration with no strategic or structural complexity. Watch for consistent dividend policy as a signal of shareholder return commitment.

OLED.brief: Universal Display Corp filed an 8-K announcing a $400 million share repurchase program authorized by its board, in addition to first-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings. The repurchase is open-market, with no fixed expiration date. As an issuer buyback, this signals capital return to shareholders amid measured near-term market conditions but long-term OLED growth. No financial advisor or premium is specified. Watch execution pace and any insider selling patterns for capital allocation signaling.

CWEN-A.brief: NYSE filed Form 25-NSE to delist Clearway Energy, Inc. Class A common stock effective May 12, 2026. Under a Certificate of Amendment effective May 1, 2026, each Class A share automatically converts into one new Class C common share, resulting in a substitution of securities. The delisting is pursuant to Rule 12d2-2(a)(3) as the Class A shares now represent only the right to receive the Class C shares; no cash payment or premium is involved. The company suspended trading on May 1. The risk-arb angle: monitor conversion mechanics and whether Class C shares will list on a national exchange or trade over-the-counter.

FHN.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed Form 25-NSE to delist and deregister First Horizon Corp's Depositary Shares (each representing a 1/400th interest in Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series C) due to full redemption, maturity, or retirement on May 1, 2026. Redemption funds were deposited and made available to holders on the same date. Trading was suspended effective May 1, with delisting effective May 12, 2026. This is a routine event-driven delisting for a called security; no premium, board recommendation, or deal structure applies. No risk-arb angle as there is no pending merger or contested event.

AUB.brief: Atlantic Union Bankshares Corp filed an 8-K announcing a $250 million share repurchase program and a quarterly dividend of $0.37 per common share. The buyback may be executed via open market or private transactions, including Rule 10b5-1 plans, through May 5, 2027. Management has discretion over timing and amounts; the program is non-binding. The board declared dividends on common and Series A preferred stock. This is an ordinary capital allocation action; no takeover/merger or activist campaign. Watch for repurchase pace and any acceleration if shares trade at a discount to tangible book value.

GHC.brief: On May 1, 2026, Graham Holdings Co disclosed via Form 8-K that its subsidiary Kaplan closed the sale of the Kaplan Languages Group (KLG). No purchase price, premium, or buyer name is disclosed; the company preliminarily expects a $60 million U.S. income tax benefit in 2026 from the transaction. No board recommendation or advisors are named. The filing is minimal, serving as a closing notice under Item 8.01. Watch for subsequent quarterly filings to reveal after-tax gain and any earnout terms; risk-arb spread is not calculable without price terms.

INDB.brief: Independent Bank Corp announced a $200 million stock buyback plan authorized by its Board effective April 30, 2026. Repurchases will commence after completion of the $10.5 million remaining under a July 2025 plan, with open-market and private transactions and Rule 10b5-1 plans. The program expires April 29, 2027, and may be modified or discontinued. No pricing details were provided beyond the aggregate authorization. The filing is an 8-K Item 8.01 Other Events. This is a routine capital return announcement; no special-situation activating events such as a tender offer or going-private transaction are involved.

LYB.brief: LyondellBasell Industries N.V. filed an 8-K reporting an amendment to its structured accounts receivables facility (Eighth Amendment to Receivables Purchase Agreement). The amendment extends the facility term to June 25, 2027, reduces the maximum amount from $900M to $700M, and updates terms to align with the company's senior unsecured revolving credit facility. No trade receivable purchases or letters of credit were outstanding as of the filing date. This is a routine financing arrangement modification, not a special situation event. There are no deal terms, premiums, or advisor involvement.

OC.brief: Owens Corning filed an 8-K on April 30, 2026, disclosing the completion of the sale of substantially all of its global glass reinforcements business to affiliates of the Praana Group (Triumph Composites Private Limited and 3B Lux S.r.l.). The enterprise value was revised downward from $755 million to $645 million via an amendment on April 14, 2026. Net after-tax cash proceeds are expected to be approximately $280 million. The company intends to use proceeds for organic growth and shareholder returns. No board recommendation or advisors are named. The transaction closed on April 30, 2026. Watch for execution of capital allocation plans and potential reinvestment or buyback announcements.

RGA.brief: Reinsurance Group of America filed an 8-K announcing full redemption of its $400M 5.75% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Subordinated Debentures due 2056 (CUSIP RZB). Redemption effective June 15, 2026 at 100% of principal plus accrued interest. No board recommendation or advisor named; redemption is mandatory under indenture terms. The notice triggers a debt reduction and lower interest expense, representing a capital return to debtholders at par.
