Watch for any refinancing plans or balance-sheet deleveraging signals from management; typical risk-arb is minimal as redemption is at par with no premium.

WT.brief: WisdomTree filed an 8-K reporting privately negotiated repurchases of $51.9M aggregate principal of its 3.25% Convertible Senior Notes due 2029 for ~$87.3M cash (a premium over par reflecting the conversion value). The transactions, expected to close June 1, 2026, will leave $18.1M of the Notes outstanding. No tender offer is used; these are issuer-initiated repurchases to reduce leverage/conversion overhang, not a formal debt tender. The filing lacks board recommendation or advisor roles. Watch for the closing condition and potential impact on diluted share count; the premium indicates embedded conversion economics.

CWK.brief: Cushman & Wakefield Ltd. filed an 8-K announcing that its wholly-owned subsidiary, the Issuer, elected to partially redeem $100 million of its outstanding $650 million 6.750% Senior Secured Notes due May 2028. The redemption price is 100% of principal plus accrued interest, with the redemption date set for May 15, 2026. This is a debt reduction / capital return move; no board recommendation, advisor, or premium. The trustee, Wilmington Trust, will execute the notice. Watch for further liability management or potential refinancing. Risk-arb angle: None; it is a straightforward partial redemption.

DRH.brief: DiamondRock Hospitality Co filed an 8-K on May 4, 2026, announcing the sale of its leasehold interest in the Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan/Fifth Avenue. The filing includes a press release and investor presentation but does not disclose specific terms such as price, premium, or buyer. The company is a hotel REIT divesting an asset. No board recommendation, advisor names, or regulatory clock are mentioned. As a non-US filing, this is equivalent to an 8-K for material definitive agreement disclosure. Watch for future disclosures on the transaction price and any potential use of proceeds for debt reduction or reinvestment.

INDV.brief: Indivior Pharmaceuticals filed an 8-K on May 4, 2026, disclosing entry into an accelerated share repurchase (ASR) agreement with Barclays Bank PLC to repurchase $175 million of its common stock under a previously authorized $400 million buyback program. The company paid the prepayment amount and received an initial delivery of 3,717,473 shares. Final settlement, based on volume-weighted average prices less a discount, is expected by June 22, 2026, with potential additional shares or cash adjustment. The filing indicates a commitment to returning capital to shareholders, typical of special-situation capital returns.

LSCC.brief: Lattice Semiconductor filed an 8-K announcing its acquisition of AMI TopCo, Inc. for total consideration of $1 billion in cash and approximately $650 million in Lattice common stock, subject to customary adjustments. The stock component ranges from about 5.2 to 6.1 million shares based on Lattice's pre-closing trading price. The merger agreement includes customary representations, warranties, termination rights, and an escrow for potential adjustments or indemnification. A registration rights agreement with THL AMI Aggregator, LP provides for two underwritten block trades. Closing is conditioned on HSR antitrust clearance. The deal combines cash and stock, with a collar mechanism on share count. Watch for regulatory timing and potential synergies in the semiconductor space.

UDR.brief: UDR, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing its Board authorized a 25 million share increase to its existing buyback program, making total authorization ~30 million shares (over $1 billion at current prices). Repurchases may occur via open-market, block, or private deals with no expiration date. The filing is a straightforward capital return announcement; board recommendation is implicit given the authorization. No advisor was named. The existing January 2008 program is unchanged. The filing does not involve a merger, tender offer, activist campaign, or strategic review. What to watch: pace of execution and any impact on share price and capital allocation strategy.

ZION.brief: Zions Bancorporation filed an 8-K reporting the sale of 460,153 Class B-1 shares of Visa Inc. on May 4, 2026, for $215 million in aggregate proceeds, generating a pre-tax gain of approximately the same amount in Q2 2026. The shares were originally received in 2007 from a Visa restructuring and IPO. No board recommendation, advisors, premium, or deal mechanics are disclosed as this is a portfolio asset sale, not a corporate action. Watch for any subsequent disclosures on capital deployment of the gain; no risk-arb angle applies.

EXEL.brief: Exelixis filed an 8-K reporting Q1 2026 earnings and announcing a new stock repurchase authorization of up to $750 million by December 31, 2027. The board authorized the buyback, enhancing existing capital return programs. No specific price or premium is stated. The program is open-market, with mechanics typical of discretionary repurchases. The filing is primarily an earnings release with a supplementary buyback announcement. Watch for execution pace and potential impact on share count and EPS.

RVTY.brief: Revvity filed an 8-K announcing the probable sale of all assets of its Immunodiagnostics business in China (China IDX) pursuant to a letter of intent signed April 16, 2026. Terms include up to $200 million, subject to adjustments and conditions. Management deems the transaction probable to close in 2027 and includes unaudited pro forma financials. No board recommendation or advisor named. Watch for regulatory approvals and adjustments to the purchase price; risk-arb focuses on execution and closing timeline.

MMM.brief: 3M Company filed an 8-K reporting its subsidiary, Fire Safety Platform Holdco, Inc., entered into a credit agreement for a $1.43 billion term loan facility and a $200 million revolving credit facility. The proceeds will finance the acquisition of Madison Safety Flow Holdings LLC from Madison Industries. The facilities mature 364 days after closing, extendable by up to 12 months. 3M guarantees the borrower's liabilities. Terms of the acquisition itself (price, premium, etc.) are not disclosed. The filing establishes the debt financing for a pending acquisition. Watch for further details on the target and regulatory clearance.

AORT.brief: Artivion, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing the completion of its acquisition of Endospan Ltd., an Israeli aortic-stability-device company. The base purchase price was $175.0 million, paid entirely in cash, with a net payment of approximately $131.3 million after offsetting intercompany loans. Contingent consideration of up to $200.0 million is payable based on future milestones. The transaction was executed via a Securities Purchase Option Agreement dated September 11, 2019, as amended. Escrow accounts of $16.5 million (indemnity) and $1.0 million (adjustment) were established. No board recommendation or advisor is named. Artivion financed the deal from internal sources. The acquisition closed immediately upon filing. Watch for integration of the Nexus product line and potential milestone achievements triggering contingent payments.

BBT.brief: Beacon Financial Corp filed an 8-K under Item 8.01 to inform stockholders that it will propose a charter amendment at the next annual meeting to allow director removal with or without cause by a majority vote, aligning with DGCL Section 141(k). No financial terms, stake percentage, premium, or advisor are mentioned. The board decided not to call a special meeting due to cost. This is a governance update, not a special-situation event such as a merger or activist campaign. No deal mechanics or risk-arb angle apply.

GEN.brief: Gen Digital Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing financial results and a Board-approved restructuring program on May 5, 2026. The restructuring aims to streamline operations and adopt AI technologies, with expected charges of ~$50M implemented over twelve months. This is an internal cost-reduction initiative; no acquisition, divestiture, or other special situation event is identified. The restructuring is described as part of ongoing transformation efforts, with estimates subject to change. The disclosure is strategic, but lacks specific details like job cuts or advisors, and the program is not a standalone event typically triggering a major category. Watch for future updates on costs and timing.

LTH.brief: Life Time Group Holdings, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a share repurchase from affiliates of Leonard Green, TPG, and Partners Group. The company bought 2,192,500 shares at ~$28.60 each for ~$62.7 million in a private transaction. The repurchase was authorized under a board-approved stock buyback program from February 2026. Mechanics: the deal was a private sale exempt from registration, reducing overhang from large sponsors. What to watch: the company may continue repurchases under its existing program; no premium or discount relative to market was disclosed, so the risk-arb angle is minimal.

ON.brief: On June 25, 2026, ON Semiconductor (onsemi) filed an 8-K announcing a definitive agreement to acquire Synaptics via a merger. Under the terms, each Synaptics share will be exchanged for 1.350 shares of onsemi common stock, implying Synaptics equityholders will own ~12% of the combined company. The onsemi Board unanimously approved the deal; no appraisal rights are available. Synaptics stock will be delisted from Nasdaq post-close. The transaction is structured as a stock-for-stock merger. The filing did not state a premium or fixed price. The close depends on regulatory and shareholder approvals; the risk-arb spread hinges on relative stock movements and deal completion timing.

PCTY.brief: Paylocity Holding Corp filed an 8-K on May 7, 2026, announcing its board approved a $1 billion increase to its existing share repurchase program, supplementing the $350 million remaining as of March 31, 2026. The program allows repurchases via open market, 10b5-1 plans, or private transactions, with timing and amount dependent on market conditions and other factors. No specific price or expiration was set; the program does not obligate repurchase of any shares and may be modified or suspended. This capital return signals management's view of undervaluation; watch for actual buyback pace to gauge commitment.

POST.brief: Post Holdings filed an 8-K disclosing the planned transition of President/CEO Robert V. Vitale to Executive Chairman, effective October 1, 2026, and the appointment of COO Nicolas Catoggio as President/CEO. The board approved the changes on May 5, 2026. No deal terms are provided as this is a management succession event. The filing also includes routine quarterly earnings results. The transition is orderly with sufficient notice, making this a forced/planned departure rather than abrupt. Watch for any strategic shifts under new leadership or potential related activism.

AGNT.brief: eXp World Holdings filed an 8-K announcing it acquired NextHome, Inc., a national real estate franchise, effective May 7, 2026. The acquisition integrates NextHome's franchise model with eXp's cloud-based brokerage, forming a multi-model platform for real estate professionals. No financial terms (price, premium, consideration) were disclosed. eXp also announced a ticker change from EXPI to AGNT, effective May 8, 2026. NextHome's management will continue leading the franchise. The filing lacks structural details or advisor names. Watch for future disclosures on purchase price, accretion, and integration progress; the deal signals a strategic pivot to a hybrid franchise/cloud model.

ADT.brief: ADT Inc. filed an 8-K reporting that three Apollo-designated directors resigned after Apollo sold all remaining shares via a secondary offering. Under an underwriting agreement dated May 4, 2026, Selling Stockholders (Apollo entities) sold 102,000,366 shares; concurrently, ADT repurchased 29,142,961 shares from underwriters under its existing $1.5 billion buyback plan. The offering and repurchase closed May 5, 2026. Bylaws were amended to remove Apollo-related references. No terms (price, premium, etc.) are stated in this excerpt. Watch for future capital allocation updates and potential ownership stabilization.

APG.brief: APi Group Corp (NYSE: APG) filed an 8-K announcing a $500M senior unsecured notes offering by its wholly owned subsidiary APi Group DE, Inc. to fund acquisitions of Onyx-Fire Protection Services and Wtech Fire Group, plus an amendment to its existing credit agreement to extend Term Loan B maturity to 2033 and upsize the revolver to $1.0B maturing 2031. The notes are offered under Rule 144A/Regulation S. No specific terms, pricing, or advisor named in excerpt. What to watch: market reception of the notes offering and timing of the acquisitions.

ITRI.brief: Itron, Inc. filed an 8-K on 8 May 2026 reporting that its board authorized a new $200M share repurchase program on 6 May 2026, effective 8 May 2026, over 18 months. Repurchases will be made in open market or via Rule 10b5-1 plans, complying with Rule 10b-18. No price per share, premium, or advisor is stated. The program is discretionary and may be suspended without notice. This is a capital-return event as the issuer directly returns cash to shareholders via buybacks. Watch for execution pace and any trading suspensions.

ALV.brief: Autoliv (issuer) filed an 8-K reporting management approval of a plan to close its manufacturing plants in Türkiye, ceasing steering wheel, airbag, and seatbelt production. The expected pre-tax charge is ~$142M (Q2 2026), with ~$129M cash costs for severance and $13M non-cash write-offs. Annual pre-tax benefit of ~$40M is anticipated from 2027, fully realized by 2028, with ~2,200 employees reduced. The plan addresses excess EMEA capacity. Watch for execution risk in the Turkish Lira currency exposure and regulatory/timing aspects of the closures.

RITM.brief: Rithm Capital Corp. filed an 8-K announcing a private offering of $500 million in senior unsecured notes due 2031. The proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, possibly including debt repayment. The notes are offered to qualified institutional buyers under Rule 144A and to non-U.S. persons under Regulation S. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The offering is unregistered and lacks exchange or registration rights. Structurally, this is a debt capital raising, not a return of capital; classification as a capital return is tentative. Watch for pricing terms and use of proceeds allocation.

SITM.brief: SiTime Corporation filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its acquisition of certain timing business assets from Renesas Electronics America Inc. The deal closed on July 1, 2026, for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $1.5 billion in cash plus 3,558,691 shares of SiTime common stock. The cash portion was funded through cash on hand. Concurrently, SiTime entered into a $200 million senior secured revolving credit facility with Wells Fargo as agent. The board recommended the transaction. The acquisition expands SiTime's product portfolio in the semiconductor timing market, and the stock component creates ongoing exposure to SiTime's performance.

TNL.brief: Travel + Leisure Co. filed an 8-K regarding a $900M private offering of 6.250% senior secured notes due 2031. Net proceeds will redeem all $650M of its outstanding 6.625% secured notes due July 2026, repay borrowings under its secured revolver, and for general corporate purposes. The offering is expected to close May 20, 2026, with redemption conditioned on consummation. This is a liability management transaction, restructuring debt capital rather than an acquisition or divestiture. Watch for closing conditions and redemption execution.

AOSL.brief: Alpha & Omega Semiconductor Ltd filed an 8-K reporting the completion of a sale of approximately 20.3% equity interest in its Chongqing joint venture (power semiconductor packaging, testing, and wafer fabrication) to SIMIC Holdings Co., Ltd. for aggregate cash consideration of $150 million, paid in four installments. The transaction closed on May 11, 2026, when the final installment was received. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The sale was previously disclosed in a July 2025 agreement, and no pro forma financials were provided as the interest was not significant. Watch for future operational or strategic shifts post-divestiture.

COLL.brief: Collegium Pharmaceutical filed an 8-K on May 12, 2026, announcing the closing of its acquisition of AZSTARYS, a CNS stimulant for ADHD, via the purchase of all membership interests in GPC Commave Holding, LLC and Commave Sub, LLC from Corium Therapeutics Holdings and Corium, LLC. The aggregate consideration was ~$650 million in cash, funded by ~$350 million cash on hand and $300 million from a delayed-draw term loan under a syndicated credit facility. Upside milestone payments of up to $135 million are contingent on AZSTARYS achieving commercial and manufacturing targets. The board had previously approved the transaction; no advisor named. The deal closed on schedule with no regulatory overhang. Watch for future milestone triggers and integration execution.

JKHY.brief: Jack Henry & Associates filed an 8-K reporting that its Board approved adding 5 million shares to its existing stock repurchase authorization, increasing the total authorization to 6.4 million shares (from 1.4 million remaining). The company has repurchased just over 2 million shares in fiscal year 2026. The buyback program, initiated in October 2002 and increased eight times, will be funded with available cash or short-term borrowings. No price targets or timetables are set. The move signals management's confidence in operations and commitment to shareholder returns. Watch for execution pace and impact on EPS.

LVS.brief: Las Vegas Sands Corp. completed an underwritten public offering of $500M 5.300% Senior Notes due 2031 and $500M 5.650% Senior Notes due 2033. Net proceeds, with cash on hand, will redeem the $1.0B 3.500% Senior Notes due August 2026, pay fees, and for general corporate purposes. The unsecured notes are senior obligations with no subsidiary guarantees, issued under a 2019 indenture supplemented by tenth and eleventh supplemental indentures. Interest is semi-annual; redemption prior to par call dates is at present value. Watch for the August 2026 note redemption execution and potential impact on leverage ratios.

SHC.brief: Sotera Health filed an 8-K reporting the termination of its Stockholders Agreement following a secondary offering by its sponsors, Warburg Pincus and GTCR. The Selling Stockholders sold 31,838,253 shares at $15.168 per share via an underwritten deal with Goldman Sachs. The company received no proceeds. The sponsors' exit triggered the termination of special governance rights, though sponsor-designated directors may remain until term end. This is a capital markets exit event, not a special situation like a going-private or activist campaign. What to watch: any resultant board governance changes or potential for a future strategic review now that sponsor overhang is removed.

AEP.brief: American Electric Power Company (AEP) disclosed entry into forward sale agreements covering 23,543,308 shares of its common stock, at an initial forward sale price of $124.968 per share, in conjunction with an underwritten public offering. The forward purchasers are Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, and Morgan Stanley. AEP expects to physically settle on or before May 31, 2028, receiving net proceeds at that time. The transaction functions as an equity forward, allowing AEP to lock in current pricing while deferring share issuance. This is a capital return mechanism for the issuer. The key watchpoint is AEP's discretion on settlement timing; early settlement may indicate near-term capital need.

CSX.brief: CSX Corporation filed an 8-K on May 14, 2026, reporting two items: Item 5.02 (departure of a named officer) and Item 5.07 (Annual Meeting voting results). CFO Stephen Fortune separated immediately, eligible for severance under a prior plan; Steve Watkins assumes his role. This officer departure appears orderly, not forced/abrupt. The meeting results show routine elections and advisory votes. No special-situation transaction is present—no M&A, tender, spin-off, activist campaign, or similar event. The filing is a routine current report covering ordinary personnel and governance matters. There is no deal, no price per share, no premium, and no regulatory or risk-arb angle to monitor. Beyond the description, no further analysis is warranted.

GIII.brief: G-III Apparel Group filed an 8-K on May 14, 2026, announcing its entry into a Unit Purchase Agreement to acquire the Marc Jacobs business from LVMH. The structure involves G-III and WHP Global forming a joint venture (IPCo) to buy Marc Jacobs Holdings, with G-III investing approximately $500 million from cash on hand and its revolving credit facility. Post-closing, G-III will operate the Marc Jacobs business under a license from IPCo, which retains the intellectual property. The closing is subject to customary conditions, including antitrust approvals, with an outside date of six months. Watch for regulatory clearance and the joint venture's operational mechanics.

JBTM.brief: JBT Marel Corp filed an 8-K/A to correct the effective date of a previously announced share repurchase program of up to $200 million of its common stock, moving the start from June 1, 2026, to May 18, 2026, through May 31, 2029. The board authorized the program at its discretion, subject to market conditions. The filing also notes a quarterly dividend of $0.10 per share payable June 9, 2026. No premium, advisors, or structural details were mentioned. Watch for execution pace and potential impact on share price, though no risk-arb angle exists as this is a standard capital return authorization.

GLW.brief: Corning Inc. had its 3.875% Notes due 2026 redeemed at maturity on May 15, 2026, as notified by the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) via Form 25-NSE. The entire class of notes was paid at par and retired. NYSE filed the removal from listing and registration, effective at the opening on May 26, 2026, under Rule 12d2-2(a)(2). Trading was suspended on May 15. There is no board recommendation, advisor, or premium. No collateral or ownership split applies. The removal is purely administrative; no risk-arb angle as this is a debt maturity, not an M&A event.

COLB.brief: Columbia Banking System, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing its Board approved a quarterly cash dividend of $0.37 per common share, payable June 15, 2026 to shareholders of record as of May 29, 2026. The dividend is a recurring capital return event, not a special situation. No M&A, activist, restructuring, or other special-situations catalyst is present. The filing includes a press release as Exhibit 99.1. What to watch: no risk-arb angle; monitor future dividend declarations for sustainability or changes.

MNST.brief: Monster Beverage Corporation filed an 8-K reporting its annual meeting results and a new $500M share repurchase authorization. The Board authorized an additional $500M buyback on May 14, 2026, supplementing the ~$400M remaining from the prior program. Repurchases may occur in open-market or negotiated transactions. No price, premium, or expiration date were specified. There is no independent advisor or premium disclosed, signaling ordinary-course capital allocation. The filing also includes uncontested director elections and routine advisory votes. Watch for the pace of repurchases as a signal of management's view on intrinsic value; no risk-arb angle as this is a straight buyback, not an issuer tender.

AKAM.brief: Akamai Technologies filed an 8-K reporting the completion of a $3.5 billion convertible note offering: $1.75 billion in 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2030 and $1.75 billion in 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2032, sold in a private placement to QIBs under Rule 144A. Net proceeds partially funded a $236.6 million convertible note hedge (offset by warrant proceeds) and a $350 million share repurchase of 2,476,298 shares. Remaining proceeds will fund accelerated CIS capital expenditures. Notes are senior unsecured obligations. The simultaneous debt issuance and stock buyback represent a capital return to shareholders via leverage. Watch for dilution impact from potential conversion and any rating agency actions.

EZPW.brief: EZCORP filed an 8-K reporting it acquired the remaining 12.3% of Founders One, LLC membership interests on May 14, 2026, achieving 100% ownership, and on May 15, 2026, through Founders, bought 1,360.65 shares of Simple Management Group (SMG) from minority holders, raising its SMG stake to 93%. No price per share, premium, or total deal value was disclosed. The board did not make a recommendation and no advisors were named. The transaction had no regulatory clock; it closed immediately. What to watch: EZCORP may seek full ownership of SMG in the near future.

FLG.brief: Flagstar Bank filed an 8-K announcing planned leadership updates on May 18, 2026. CEO Joseph M. Otting will relinquish the President role while continuing as Executive Chairman and CEO. Richard Raffetto and Lee Smith, both Senior Executive Vice Presidents, were appointed Co-Presidents and Co-COOs, with Raffetto becoming Chief Banking Officer and Smith remaining CFO. Bao Nguyen was elevated to Chief Legal Officer. These changes are part of the bank's succession planning and strategic realignment. Terms include no purchase price or premium. Watch for further organizational shifts as the bank executes its long-term strategy.

LIF.brief: Life360 filed an 8-K reporting that its Board authorized a $225 million share repurchase program. The program allows open-market, privately negotiated, and block-trade buybacks, possibly under Rule 10b5-1 plans. No specific price, premium, or close date is given; the program is multi-year and aims to offset stock-based compensation dilution. The company cites a strong balance sheet and 12 consecutive quarters of positive operating cash flow. Repurchases may be modified or suspended at any time. Watch for ongoing buyback execution and potential impact on share count; no risk-arb angle as this is not a M&A event.

SAM.brief: The Boston Beer Company filed an 8-K announcing a 10b5-1 plan to repurchase up to $25 million of its Class A Common Stock during a period from June 29, 2026 to September 25, 2026. The repurchase is an issuer share buyback undertaken under a pre-arranged trading plan to allow repurchases during blackout periods. The filing includes no details on board recommendation or advisors. The mechanics are a standard 10b5-1 plan, reducing shares outstanding and returning capital to shareholders. Watch for the actual pace of repurchases and any impact on EPS.

KMT.brief: Kennametal filed an 8-K under Items 5.02, 8.01, and 9.01 announcing the appointment of Amanda Cole as Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer effective July 21, 2026, succeeding Judith Bacchus who will retire as Chief Administrative Officer on October 1, 2026. Ms. Cole joins from Wesco International and will enter into standard indemnification and officer employment agreements. No material terms such as price, premium, or deal value were disclosed. The filing is a routine officer appointment with no structural mechanics or regulatory clock, and does not constitute a special situation event.

VAL.brief: Valaris Ltd files an 8-K reporting that CFIUS clearance has been obtained for Transocean Ltd's acquisition of Valaris. Under the Business Combination Agreement dated February 9, 2026, Valaris shareholders will receive 15.235 Transocean shares per Valaris share. The deal is still subject to HSR Act clearance; a Second Request from the DOJ has been received, and the parties have agreed not to close until at least 60 days after certifying substantial compliance, expected no earlier than late September 2026. Closing remains targeted for H2 2026. The key risk-arb factor is the regulatory timeline from the DOJ Second Request.

PNC.brief: PNC Financial Services Group filed a prospectus supplement (424B5) for an offering of senior fixed/floating-rate and floating-rate notes due 2029. It is a debt capital markets transaction, not a special situation. The filing details terms, underwriting, and risk factors but involves no M&A, activist, restructuring, or other event-driven category. No deal terms are applicable. This is a routine debt issuance.

CTRE.brief: CareTrust REIT, Inc. filed an 8-K on May 18, 2026, announcing a common stock offering of 12,500,000 firm shares (plus up to 1,875,000 optional shares) at $40.225 per share to underwriters. The offering closed on May 20, 2026. Concurrently, the Company entered forward sale agreements with Wells Fargo and JPMorgan for the firm shares, under which forward sellers borrowed and sold shares, with physical settlement expected by May 20, 2027. The Company may elect cash or net share settlement. This structured equity capital raise, via forward sales, defers dilution and provides proceeds; watch for eventual settlement method and share price impact.

PRSU.brief: Pursuit Attractions & Hospitality, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing an amendment to its Equity Purchase Agreement with Flyover Attractions B.V. and Brogent Technologies, Inc. to extend the outside closing date from May 21, 2026, to July 31, 2026, for the sale of its Flyover flying theater attractions business. No price, premium, or advisor was mentioned. The amendment only modifies the deadline; other terms remain unchanged. Closing is subject to customary conditions. The extension pushes back a potential termination date, signaling ongoing regulatory or logistical hurdles. Watch for whether the deal closes by the new deadline or is terminated.

WSBC.brief: WesBanco, Inc. filed an 8-K on May 20, 2026, announcing a new stock repurchase program approved by its Board of Directors authorizing the repurchase of up to an additional 4.0 million shares of common stock, combining with 0.9 million remaining from a prior authorization for a total of 4.9 million shares, representing approximately 5.1% of shares outstanding as of March 31, 2026. The program has no expiration date and may be effected through open market purchases, privately-negotiated transactions, block trades, or Rule 10b5-1 plans, funded from existing cash and liquidity sources. The filing is a standard capital return event. Watch for execution pace against market conditions.

GTLS.brief: Baker Hughes Company completed its acquisition of Chart Industries, Inc. via merger on July 16, 2026. The NYSE filed Form 25-NSE to delist Chart common stock effective July 27, 2026. Holders received $210.00 per share in cash. The merger was unanimously recommended by Chart's board; no advisor disclosed. Each share converted into the right to receive cash. The deal had no financing contingency as Baker Hughes funded from cash. The transaction closed at the stated price with no premium disclosed. The regulatory clock ran its course. What to watch: any appraisal or dissenters' rights actions seeking a higher value.

EQR.brief: Equity Residential filed Amendment No. 1 to Form S-4 on July 9, 2026, in connection with its merger with AvalonBay Communities, Inc. announced May 20, 2026. The all-stock deal values AvalonBay at $0.442 per share and Equity Residential at 0.442 per share (subject to exchange ratio). Boards of both companies unanimously recommend the merger; Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz and Goodwin Procter serve as legal advisors. The transaction is structured as a merger of equals, with Equity Residential issuing shares to AvalonBay stockholders. Collateral includes stock exchange mechanics; no break fee disclosed. Closing expected in early 2027 pending regulatory approvals and shareholder votes. Watch for FTC clearance and shareholder meeting dates.

STX.brief: Seagate Technology Holdings plc filed an 8-K announcing the closing of privately negotiated exchange agreements with holders of its subsidiary's 3.50% Exchangeable Senior Notes due 2028. Under the exchanges, $185.908 million principal amount of notes was exchanged for $185.908 million in cash plus 2,023,124 ordinary shares of Seagate. The share count was determined over one trading day beginning May 21, 2026. The exchanges closed on May 26-27, 2026. This debt-for-equity swap reduces leverage and dilutes shareholders. No board recommendation or external advisors were disclosed. Watch for potential further liability management or impact on credit ratings.

UNM.brief: Unum Group filed an 8-K reporting that its subsidiary, Unum Life Insurance Company of America, entered a Master Transaction Agreement with Fortitude Reinsurance Company Ltd. to reinsure a portion of its closed block individual long-term care business. The agreement includes a partial recapture from a captive and a retrocession to a third-party reinsurer. Terms such as price or premium are not disclosed; statutory reserves for the reinsured business were $3.8B as of March 31, 2026. Closing is expected in 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and execution of related agreements. Watch for regulatory clearance and the final structure of the retrocession.

AMT.brief: American Tower Corp (AMT) filed an 8-K reporting the termination of its Strategic Collocation Agreement with DISH Wireless L.L.C., effective June 2, 2026. The termination notice was delivered by AMT, and DISH revenue has been fully reflected in churn since January 1, 2026, with no expected impact on 2026 financial results. AMT continues litigation against DISH regarding obligations under the agreement. This is not a special situation but a contractual termination and legal dispute.

CVCO.brief: Cavco Industries filed an 8-K (Item 8.01) announcing a $150 million stock repurchase program approved by its board on May 18, 2026. Purchases may be made in open market or privately negotiated transactions; no specific price, share count, or expiry date is set. The program is discretionary and can be suspended at any time; it will be funded by existing cash. The filing also contained fiscal Q4 and FY2026 earnings results. The buyback announcement is a non-binding capital return authorization. Watch for actual execution pace as a signal of management's view on undervaluation. There is no risk-arb angle as this is not an M&A event.

PGNY.brief: Progyny, Inc. disclosed in an 8-K that its Board approved a share repurchase program of up to $200 million of common stock. The program will be funded from available cash; repurchases may occur in the open market (including Rule 10b5-1 plans) at management's discretion based on stock price and market conditions, and may be suspended or discontinued at any time. No specific price, premium, or timeline was provided. The program does not commit the company to any particular number of shares. Watch for periodic disclosures of repurchase activity under this authorization.

APLE.brief: Apple Hospitality REIT, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting annual meeting voting results and extending its share repurchase program to July 2027 with a $242.5 million authorization. Repurchases may be made in open market, through 10b5-1 plans, or in private transactions, depending on market conditions. No advisor or board recommendation details are provided beyond the board's approval. The filing is not a routine current report, as the program extension is a capital return event. Focus on actual repurchase execution against the authorization, noting that conditions, including market conditions and other factors, may affect timing and volume.

MYRG.brief: MYR Group Inc. filed an 8-K on May 27, 2026, announcing its acquisition of all shares of Valley Holdings I, Inc. (Valley), a Washington-based electrical contractor, for approximately $328 million, subject to post-closing adjustments. The consideration is cash funded from cash on hand and revolving credit facilities. There are additional contingent payments for key executives based on performance targets. Board recommendation, advisor, and premium were not disclosed. The deal requires regulatory approval and other customary conditions. Watch for regulatory timeline and any counterbids; risk-arb focuses on financing and closing certainty.

PWR.brief: Quanta Services, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its 2026 Annual Meeting results and announcing a new stock repurchase program authorized by the Board as of May 21, 2026. The filing discloses director elections and advisory votes but does not specify the size, terms, or duration of the buyback authorization. This capital return mechanism signals a commitment to return value to shareholders, though lacking detail. Watch for a subsequent 8-K with program parameters to assess scale and execution pace.

APOG.brief: Apogee Enterprises, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its acquisition of all outstanding equity interests of Keller Companies, Inc. and its subsidiaries, including Kalwall Corporation and Structures Unlimited, Inc., for $105 million in cash at closing plus up to $10 million in contingent consideration based on future performance. The acquisition was funded with available cash and borrowings under its revolving credit facility. The board recommended the transaction; no advisor is named. The deal closed on July 1, 2026, with customary post-closing adjustments. Watch for potential earn-out achievement and integration risk as Apogee expands its architectural products portfolio.

AXTA.brief: Axalta Coating Systems Ltd. filed a definitive proxy statement for a special meeting on August 5, 2026, to approve its all-share merger of equals with Akzo Nobel N.V. Each Axalta share will be exchanged for 0.6539 AkzoNobel ordinary shares, plus a special pre-closing cash dividend of up to €2.5 billion. Based on recent prices, implied value is ~$34.36 per share. Axalta shareholders will hold ~45% of the combined entity. The board recommends voting for the deal. Post-merger, shares will trade on the NYSE and Euronext Amsterdam, with Amsterdam delisting planned ~12 months later. Key watch items: shareholder approval, regulatory clearance, and FX fluctuations affecting deal value.

H.brief: Hyatt Hotels Corp filed an 8-K announcing its Board authorized an additional $1.0 billion share repurchase program for its Class A and Class B common stock. Repurchases may occur via open market, private transactions, Rule 10b5-1 plans, or accelerated share repurchase transactions at the company's discretion, subject to market conditions and applicable law. The authorization does not obligate Hyatt to repurchase any specific amount and may be suspended or discontinued at any time. Investors should watch the pace of buyback execution and potential impact on earnings per share.

NTAP.brief: NetApp filed an 8-K reporting fiscal Q4 2026 results and announcing a $1.0B share repurchase authorization. The new buyback has no expiration date; repurchases may be executed via open-market (Rule 10b-18), 10b5-1 plans, privately-negotiated transactions, or accelerated share repurchases. No specific price per share, premium, or close date is stated. The board authorized the repurchase; no financial advisor is named. The program offers flexibility but no commitment. Watch for the pace of execution under the renewed buyback authorization; the lack of set terms leaves the rate of capital return uncertain.

PEB.brief: Pebblebrook Hotel Trust filed an 8-K reporting the sale of the 115-room Chamberlain West Hollywood Hotel in Los Angeles, CA, for $43.5 million to a third party, closing on May 27, 2026. The price reflects gross proceeds from a single property sale; no per-share price, premium, or advisor is stated. Proceeds will be used for debt reduction, preferred equity paydown, opportunistic share repurchases, and other capital allocation priorities. The sale is a straightforward asset divestiture with no special terms or regulatory clock noted. Watch for further hotel dispositions or capital return updates as part of Pebblebrook's portfolio optimization.

TSCO.brief: Tractor Supply Company (TSCO) acquired VIP Petcare (operating as VIP Petcare and PetVet) from PetIQ, a Bansk Group company, as announced in an 8-K filed May 28, 2026. VIP Petcare is the largest U.S. mobile veterinary care provider, operating in ~2,700 retail locations, including 1,700 Tractor Supply stores, serving over 1 million pets annually. Terms—price, premium, and consideration—were not disclosed. The acquisition strengthens Tractor Supply's pet health platform by integrating veterinary services, pharmacy, and retail. No board recommendation or advisors named. The deal is expected to close pending regulatory approvals; watch for integration updates and any antitrust review.

BTU.brief: Peabody Energy Corp filed an 8-K announcing the pricing of $225 million aggregate principal amount of 0.50% convertible senior notes due 2031, offered privately to qualified institutional buyers under Rule 144A. The notes are senior unsecured obligations, settle June 2, 2026, with an underwriter option for an additional $25 million. Interest is payable semi-annually; conversion rights begin December 1, 2030, with settlement in cash, stock, or a combination. This is a routine debt capital markets transaction, not a special situation. No special-situation elements are present.

CBU.brief: Community Financial System, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing the completion of its acquisition of ClearPoint Federal Bank Trust, a federally chartered savings association and leader in trust administration for the death care industry. The deal, originally announced January 14, 2026, was effected via merger with Community Bank, N.A., a wholly-owned subsidiary. ClearPoint has over $1.5 billion in assets under management and a historical three-year revenue CAGR of 9.7%. No financial terms, price per share, premium, or advisors were disclosed. The acquired business will operate as ClearPoint Trust, a division of Community Bank. Watch for integration updates and revenue contribution from Nottingham Financial Group.

EHC.brief: Encompass Health issued $500M of 5.875% Senior Notes due 2034 via a private Rule 144A/Reg S offering, netting ~$491.2M after discounts and expenses. Proceeds will redeem $400M of its 4.500% notes due 2028 at par and repay $100M under its revolver, representing a liability management / capital-return event through refinancing to lower near-term debt. The indenture with Computershare includes standard make-whole redemption provisions. No change in equity structure; watch ability to refinance remaining $400M of 2028 notes if callable. This is a debt capital return, not an equity distribution.

FCPT.brief: Four Corners Property Trust (FCPT) filed an 8-K disclosing the closing of its acquisition of 102 veterinary properties from Shore Capital Real Estate Partners Holdco, LLC for $268.0 million, based on ~$17.37 million initial annual cash rent. The purchase was via a subsidiary under a Purchase and Sale Agreement dated May 29, 2026. All properties are operated by Mission Pet Health. The all-cash deal closed July 16, 2026, with a rent credit received at closing. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The acquisition adds net-leased retail/restaurant properties to FCPT's portfolio. Watch for integration execution and cap rate accretion relative to FCPT's stated 6.6% YTD weighted average cap rate.

ORLY.brief: On June 1, 2026, O'Reilly Automotive's board approved a $2.0 billion increase to its share repurchase authorization, raising the aggregate to $31.75 billion, effective for three years. Repurchases will be made in open market transactions at prevailing prices based on market conditions and corporate factors, with no fixed timetable or obligation to buy any shares. The program may be modified, suspended, or terminated at any time. No advisor, premium, or price terms are disclosed. The filing is an 8-K Item 8.01 (Other Events) announcing expanded buyback capacity. Watch for actual repurchase cadence; the authorization signals management's view on capital allocation and undervaluation but carries no commitment.

STEP.brief: StepStone Group Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the third exchange completed May 29, 2026, acquiring ~5% equity interests in each of three Asset Class Entities (SRE, SRA, SPD) from third-party sellers. The aggregate consideration was approximately $10M cash (pre-adjustment ~$11M), 972,685 shares of Class A common stock, and 2,438,273 Class D units. Post-exchange, StepStone holdings rose to 65% in each entity. Consideration based on exchange ratios tied to estimated adjusted net income and an adjusted trading multiple. Shares and units issued unregistered under Section 4(a)(2). Watch for continued step acquisitions and potential full consolidation or future registration events.

UFPI.brief: UFP Industries Inc. filed an 8-K on June 1, 2026, announcing that its Board authorized a share repurchase program of up to $300 million of its outstanding common stock, expiring April 30, 2027. The repurchases may be executed via open market, private negotiations, or Rule 10b5-1 plans. Timing and amount depend on market conditions and share price. The company is not obligated to repurchase shares. The prior authorization was replaced. Watch for future buyback execution pace; no premium or advisor was noted.

AVA.brief: Avista Corp filed an 8-K disclosing a non-binding MOU with a developer for a large load electric service interconnection. The customer seeks 125 MW starting in 2029, expanding to 500 MW by 2032. Next steps include an Engineering and Procurement Contract, regulatory approval from the Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission, and definitive agreements. No financial terms, board recommendation, or advisors are named. This is a preliminary infrastructure development agreement, not a special situation, with no M&A or corporate action. Watch for regulatory filings and definitive agreements.

WLY.brief: John Wiley & Sons, Inc. disclosed via Form 8-K that its indirect wholly-owned subsidiary, John Wiley & Sons Ltd., entered into an Equity Purchase Agreement on June 1, 2026, to acquire all outstanding equity of CIG Emerald Midco LLC (doing business as Emerald Publishing) from CIG Emerald Midco LLC and Emerald Holding. The purchase price is GBP 337.5 million (~$452 million) in cash, funded from cash on hand. The acquisition of over 480 peer-reviewed journals and 8,000 books expands Wiley's research publishing portfolio. The filing includes customary representations, warranties, and indemnification provisions. No advisor or board recommendation is stated. Watch for closing conditions and regulatory approvals.

FCN.brief: FTI Consulting filed an 8-K disclosing its annual shareholder meeting results (routine) and a board authorization to repurchase an additional $370 million of common stock under its existing Stock Repurchase Program. The program has cumulative authorizations of $2.6 billion, with 19,104,867 shares repurchased through June 2, 2026. No specific price, premium, or timeline is given; the authorization expands available capacity. The filing is a routine capital-return disclosure, not a full self-tender or other special situation. Watch for future repurchase pace and program exhaustion.

KFY.brief: Korn Ferry filed an 8-K disclosing entry into a Sale and Purchase Agreement to acquire all shares of Auxey Holdco Limited (AMS) for ~£850 million (~$1.1 billion) through ~£659M cash and ~£191M in stock. The stock component is subject to a collar (85%-115% of $71.3815 VWAP). The deal uses a locked-box mechanism with a December 31, 2025 locked-box date and standard leakage protections. The filing does not name a board recommendation or advisor. Closing awaits regulatory and customary conditions; watch for regulatory clearance timing and collar mechanics that could shift the stock portion's value.

UNFI.brief: United Natural Foods, Inc. filed an 8-K regarding a Term Loan Amendment entered on June 18, 2026. The amendment reprices approximately $371 million outstanding term loan, reducing the applicable margin over SOFR from 4.75% to 4.00%. The Co-Borrowers include SUPERVALU INC., UNFI Wholesale, Inc., and UNFI Distribution Company, LLC. JPMorgan Chase Bank serves as administrative and collateral agent. No board recommendation or advisor is named. All other material terms remain unchanged. This is a routine debt repricing, not a special situation. Watch for potential future refinancing or leverage changes.

ETR.brief: Entergy Corp filed an 8-K reporting the physical settlement of ATM and underwritten forward sale agreements. On June 22, 2026, it delivered 2,057,826 shares under ATM forward agreements for ~$126M cash, settling all outstanding ATM forwards, and 6,650,417 shares under underwritten forward agreements for ~$546M. Post-settlement, 11,145,984 shares remain under underwritten forwards (proceeds ~$915M), plus 19,247,788 additional shares from May 5, 2026 agreements. The forward sales, disclosed in annual/quarterly reports, effectively raise capital through equity forwards. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or close date cited. Watch potential dilution impact and additional settlements.

FISV.brief: Fiserv Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the closing of a public offering of €500 million aggregate principal amount of 3.750% Senior Notes due 2030 and €500 million of 4.250% Senior Notes due 2034. The notes were issued under an existing indenture with U.S. Bank Trust Company as trustee, supplemented by a Thirty-Ninth and Fortieth Supplemental Indenture. Proceeds use is not specified; the offering expands the company's debt capital structure. This is a routine debt issuance, not a special situation. No special-situation trigger exists; watch for use of proceeds in capital allocation.

FCFS.brief: FirstCash Holdings, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing a revised recommended cash offer via its subsidiary Chess Bidco Limited to acquire Ramsdens Holdings PLC, a UK AIM-listed company. The revised offer is 684 pence per share in cash (675 pence from Bidco plus a 9 pence permitted dividend), representing aggregate consideration of approximately £229 million, increased by £26 million. The transaction is to be effected as a scheme of arrangement under UK law, requiring approval by a majority in number and 75% in value of Ramsdens shareholders, court sanction, and regulatory approvals from the UK FCA and CMA. Watch for shareholder vote and regulatory clearance timelines.

EQH.brief: Equitable Holdings filed an 8-K updating the status of a merger-of-equals with Corebridge Financial. Under the terms announced March 26, 2026, Equitable and Corebridge will merge via two subsidiary mergers, with a newly formed holding company (New Equitable) surviving and renamed Equitable Holdings. Shareholders will receive New Equitable common stock; no per-share price, premium, or break fee is disclosed. Both boards recommend the deal. The definitive joint proxy/prospectus, declared effective June 23, 2026, has been mailed; shareholder votes are pending. Watch for shareholder approval and regulatory clearance timelines.

BRBR.brief: BellRing Brands filed an 8-K on June 24, 2026, disclosing workforce realignment actions approved to streamline operations and improve efficiency. The company expects annualized run-rate operating expense savings of $10–$12 million pre-tax ($3M non-cash stock compensation), to begin in Q4 fiscal 2026 with majority in fiscal 2027. One-time charges of ~$6 million (cash severance) will be incurred primarily in Q3 fiscal 2026, with actions substantially complete by end of Q3. Separately, Chief Growth Officer Douglas J. Cornille stepped down effective June 24, 2026, with departure on September 1, 2026, receiving severance per existing plans. This restructuring is a cost-cutting reorganization, not a special situation category like a strategic review or activist campaign.

PLD.brief: Prologis filed an 8-K announcing an indicative all-share proposal to acquire SEGRO plc, a UK industrial REIT, on June 16, 2026. Terms of the all-stock transaction are not specified in terms of price per share or premium. SEGRO's board unequivocally rejected the proposal on June 23, 2026. Prologis urged SEGRO shareholders to encourage engagement. Under UK Takeover Code Rule 2.6(a), Prologis must announce a firm intention to make an offer or walk away by July 22, 2026. The filing is a non-US takeover mapped to an acquisition. Watch for Prologis's next move: a possible hostile bid or walkaway.

AZZ.brief: AZZ Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a fiscal 2027 Q1 cash dividend of $0.24/share, a 20% increase from the prior $0.20/share. The dividend is payable on July 30, 2026, to shareholders of record July 9, 2026. The Board authorized the dividend; no advisors were named. This is a routine capital return event (regular dividend), not a special situation. The filing includes a press release and inline XBRL. No risk-arb angle exists; watch for continued dividend policy as a signal of shareholder value commitment.

SYNA.brief: Synaptics Inc. filed an 8-K announcing entry into a definitive merger agreement to be acquired by ON Semiconductor Corporation (onsemi). Under the agreement, each share of Synaptics common stock will be converted into 1.350 shares of onsemi common stock (stock consideration). The merger consideration is all-stock; no per-share dollar price or premium percentage is stated. The deal is structured as a reverse triangular merger with Synaptics surviving as an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary. Board recommendation and advisors are not named in this excerpt. Regulatory approvals are subject to conditions, with no expected close date provided. Watch for shareholder vote and antitrust clearance for risk-arb spread.

OII.brief: Oceaneering International filed an 8-K announcing a private placement of $500M 6.875% Senior Notes due 2034, entered via a purchase agreement with J.P. Morgan Securities as representative of initial purchasers. The offering, exempt under Rule 144A and Regulation S, is expected to close July 6, 2026. Net proceeds, together with cash on hand, will fund the purchase of the 2028 Notes in a previously announced tender offer, representing a capital return via deleveraging/refinancing. Remaining proceeds may be used for general corporate purposes, including debt repayment or repurchase. Watch for tender offer results and interest rate environment impact.

CURB.brief: Curbline Properties Corp. filed a 424B5 preliminary prospectus supplement for a forward-sale offering of 10,000,000 common shares (up to 11,500,000 with overallotment). Shares are borrowed and sold by forward purchasers (Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo); Curbline receives proceeds only upon physical settlement within ~18 months, with option for cash or net-share settlement. The last sale price was $31.27/share. The structure defers proceeds and dilutes over time; proceeds are for general corporate purposes, not a return of capital directly. Watch forward settlement elections and any cash-settlement risk, which could reduce or eliminate proceeds. Risk-arb angle: minimal typical arbitrage, but monitor execution timing and settlement method.

DLR.brief: Digital Realty Trust, Inc. filed an 8-K describing the creation of non-voting common stock in connection with the closing of the Blackstone Acquisition, making Digital Realty the target. The filing references Articles Supplementary designating 12,310,249 shares as non-voting common stock, which convert to voting common stock upon transfer by the initial holder or affiliate. No specific price, premium, advisor, or board recommendation is stated. The mechanical detail is the automatic conversion feature tied to transfer. Key watchpoint: regulatory approvals and integration timeline for the Blackstone deal, with risk-arb focus on deal completion conditions and any potential shareholder dissent.

MTX.brief: Minerals Technologies Inc. (MTI) filed a Plan of Reorganization in Chapter 11 cases of its subsidiaries BMI OldCo Inc. and affiliated debtors, as announced via press release on June 29, 2026. The filing complies with a court deadline. No specific financial terms (stake, price, premium) are disclosed. The board is not explicitly recommending, and no advisors are named. Mechanically, the plan involves non-debtor affiliates; the bankruptcy proceedings are in the Southern District of Texas. Watch for court approval and potential creditor negotiations; risk-arb centers on plan confirmation and exit financing terms.

LCII.brief: LCI Industries entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with Patrick Industries and two merger subs. Under the terms, each LCI share will be converted into 1.2440 shares of Patrick common stock (stock consideration). Post-closing, pre-merger Patrick shareholders will own about 52% of the combined entity; LCI shareholders the remainder. Both boards unanimously approved the transaction. The deal involves a two-step merger structure, with First Merger Sub merging into LCI, then the surviving entity merging into Second Merger Sub. Watch for shareholder votes, regulatory clearances, and the exchange ratio adjustment mechanics.

PATK.brief: Patrick Industries (PATK) filed an 8-K on June 30, 2026, announcing its acquisition of LCI Industries via a two-step merger structure. Under the Agreement and Plan of Merger, each LCI share will be converted into 1.2440 shares of PATK common stock (stock consideration). Post-closing, PATK shareholders will own ~52% and former LCI shareholders ~48% of the combined company. The boards of both companies unanimously approved the transaction. The filing does not specify a premium, closing date, or break fee. Watch for regulatory clearance and shareholder votes; risk-arb spread will reflect execution timeline and stock consideration volatility.

TALO.brief: Talos Energy Inc. filed an 8-K reporting entry into an indenture for $800M 8.000% second-priority senior secured notes due 2034. Proceeds will partially fund its pending Gulf of America acquisition of oil and gas assets (Na Kika and Coulomb fields) from Shell Offshore Inc., redeem its outstanding 9.000% notes due 2029, and pay fees. The acquisition is subject to a purchase agreement dated June 30, 2026, with an outside date for closing. The notes are secured by collateral and guaranteed by subsidiaries. Watch for regulatory clearance and timely closing; risk-arb focuses on financing completion and asset integration.

ABR.brief: Arbor Realty Trust Inc. filed an 8-K to report the issuance and sale of $375M aggregate principal amount of 6.25% Convertible Senior Notes due 2029, including full exercise of the initial purchasers' option for an additional $50M. The notes are senior unsecured, bear 6.25% interest payable semiannually, and mature July 1, 2029; they are convertible prior to April 1, 2029 upon satisfaction of conditions and anytime thereafter. Upon conversion, the company will settle in cash and/or common stock at its election. The initial conversion rate is 164.0016 shares per $1,000 principal, equivalent to ~$6.10 per share. No redemption or sinking fund is provided. This is a capital-return transaction via convertible note offering; watch for dilution upon conversion and interest payment obligations.

ES.brief: Eversource Energy filed an 8-K announcing the completed sale of its subsidiary Aquarion Water Company to Aquarion Water Authority, a Connecticut quasi-public entity, for $2.4 billion in cash. The sale was executed after satisfying all regulatory terms and requirements. Adjusted net equity proceeds of approximately $1.7 billion will be used to displace Eversource debt. The company expects a non-cash after-tax charge of ~$115 million ($0.31/share) in Q2 2026. No board recommendation, advisor, break fee, or premium was disclosed. The filing is a closing announcement, not a pending transaction. What to watch: the deployment of proceeds and any impact on credit ratings.

KR.brief: Kroger Co. filed an 8-K announcing it has entered into a merger agreement to acquire Giant Eagle, Inc. for approximately $1.65 billion, consisting of $1.25 billion in cash and $400 million in assumed liabilities. The acquisition is expected to close in 2027, subject to HSR antitrust clearance and customary conditions. Kroger anticipates limited store divestitures to satisfy regulatory requirements. No board recommendation or advisor is named in the filing. Risk-arb watchers should monitor the antitrust review timeline and potential store sale process.

AA.brief: Alcoa Corp filed an 8-K disclosing its entry into an Umbrella Implementation Deed to acquire South32 Limited's bauxite, alumina, and aluminum smelting operations. The aggregate upfront consideration is $3.1 billion in cash plus approximately 17 million shares of Alcoa common stock valued at about $1 billion (based on a $58.79/share 10-day VWAP), representing ~6% post-issuance ownership. Alcoa also agrees to pay up to $750 million in cash as a contingent value right based on alumina/aluminum prices over four annual periods. The transaction is subject to South32 shareholder approval, regulatory clearances, and other customary conditions, with closing expected in the first half of 2027. A termination fee of $41M or $82M is payable by South32 in certain circumstances. Watch for shareholder vote and regulatory timelines.

KRG.brief: Kite Realty Group, L.P. issued $345 million (with a $45 million greenshoe fully exercised for $390 million total) of 3.25% Exchangeable Senior Notes due 2032 in a private placement under Rule 144A. The notes are senior unsecured obligations of the operating partnership, issued under an indenture with U.S. Bank Trust as trustee. The proceeds likely support capital-return activities such as share buybacks or debt reduction. Exchangeability and conversion mechanics are not detailed. Watch for potential dilution or balance sheet restructuring impacts on equity value.

SXI.brief: Standex International, via its Singaporean subsidiary Mold-Tech Singapore, filed an 8-K reporting entry into a Securities Purchase Agreement on June 26, 2026 to acquire the remaining 9.90% of Narayan Powertech Private Limited from minority shareholders. This follows a prior 90.10% acquisition on October 28, 2024, where the second closing via share swap was contingent on RBI approval which was not obtained by October 28, 2025, triggering put/call options. Instead, parties negotiated a direct sale. No price, premium, or advisor disclosed. Watch for closing conditions and regulatory clearance in India.

CXW.brief: CoreCivic, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the sale of two detention facilities to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security. The California City Detention Facility (2,560 beds) sold for ~$732.6M, and the Otay Mesa Detention Center (1,994 beds) for ~$739.2M, both closed concurrently on July 2, 2026. Terms include cash consideration; no premium or board recommendation cited. CoreCivic expects to continue managing the facilities under existing ICE contracts. The transaction is a government asset acquisition, removing over 4,500 beds from CoreCivic's owned portfolio. Watch for subsequent management contract modifications and potential capital deployment from the ~$1.47B in proceeds.

ESI.brief: Element Solutions Inc, a specialty chemicals company, entered into a definitive merger agreement with Solstice Advanced Materials Inc. Under the agreement, Solar Merger Sub One will merge with Element Solutions, making it a wholly-owned subsidiary of Solstice, followed by a second merger. The boards of both companies unanimously approved the transaction. The merger consideration is Solstice Common Stock, structured as a tax-free reorganization under Section 368(a). The filing does not disclose specific financial terms. The transaction is subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. Risk-arb investors should watch for antitrust clearance and stockholder votes.

EXR.brief: Extra Space Storage Inc. (EXR), a real estate investment trust, filed an 8-K disclosing that its subsidiary Extra Space Storage LP completed an underwritten public offering of $550M aggregate principal amount of 4.900% Senior Notes due 2032. The notes were priced at 99.702% of par and are fully guaranteed by the parent and two holding trusts. Interest is payable semi-annually. The indenture contains restrictive covenants including limitations on additional indebtedness and unencumbered asset requirements. This is a routine debt capital markets transaction, not a special situation. No acquisition, divestiture, activist, strategic review, tender, going-private, capital return, spin-off, rights offering, restructuring, liquidation, delisting, issuer tender, deal termination, SPAC, or management change is involved.

SMTC.brief: Semtech Corp filed an 8-K regarding entry into a new $360 million revolving credit facility, which was undrawn at closing, and an uncommitted incremental term loan facility. The proceeds are for working capital, general corporate purposes, refinancing existing debt, and funding permitted acquisitions. The revolving facility matures July 6, 2031 with a springing maturity tied to outstanding 2030 convertible notes. The filing does not announce a specific capital return event; the new credit line could support future shareholder returns, but no immediate return is stated. The conservative categorization is None, as this is a routine refinancing and financing agreement, not a special situation.

USPH.brief: USPH filed an 8-K announcing the acquisition of a twelve-clinic physical therapy practice effective July 1, 2026. USPH acquired a 67% equity interest with 33% retained by current owners. The practice generates ~112,000 annual visits and $12 million in annual revenue. No price per share, premium, or advisor was disclosed. The transaction is structured as a partial acquisition with ongoing owner involvement. Watch for clinic integration and state expansion strategy. No risk-arb angle due to lack of public target or deal premium.

BF-B.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed a Form 25-NSE notifying the SEC of its intention to remove from listing and registration the 1.200% Notes due 2026 of Brown-Forman Corp. The entire class of notes was redeemed or paid at maturity on July 7, 2026, and suspended from trading that same day, with delisting effective July 20, 2026. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or ownership details apply as this is a debt maturity event. The rationale is contractual redemption at par. What to watch: no risk-arb angle; the notes are extinguished.

VRTX.brief: Vertex Pharmaceuticals filed an 8-K announcing a definitive merger agreement to acquire Crinetics Pharmaceuticals for $85.00 per share in cash. Vertex is the acquirer through its wholly owned subsidiary, Clark Merger Sub. The transaction implies a total equity value of approximately $6.5 billion based on Crinetics' diluted shares. Consideration is all cash, with a premium of roughly 50% over Crinetics' last unaffected close. The board of Crinetics recommended the deal. Closing requires majority shareholder approval, HSR clearance, and no legal restraint. Outstanding unvested options and RSUs automatically vest and are cashed out. Watch for stockholder vote, antitrust review timeline, and any competing bids—risk-arb spreads will reflect regulatory and execution risk.

EPAC.brief: Enerpac Tool Group Corp. filed an 8-K regarding its entry into a merger agreement to acquire Specialized Fabrication Equipment Group LLC (SFE Group) for approximately $451.4 million in cash via a merger of its subsidiary Merger Sub with and into SFE Group, which will become a wholly owned subsidiary. Consideration is subject to customary closing adjustments and transaction expenses. The transaction is subject to regulatory approvals and other customary conditions. No board recommendation or advisor was mentioned. The acquisition is all-cash. Watch for regulatory clearance and closing conditions; the risk-arb spread will depend on deal certainty and timeline.

FHB.brief: First Hawaiian, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing entry into a merger agreement to acquire TriCo Bancshares. Under the terms, TriCo shareholders will receive 2.095 FHI shares per TriCo share (stock consideration). The boards of both companies unanimously approved the transaction. The deal structure involves two steps: Merger Sub merges into TriCo, then the surviving entity merges into FHI, followed by a bank merger of Tri Counties Bank into First Hawaiian Bank. Equity awards will be converted into FHI shares based on performance achievement. The filing does not specify a premium, expected close date, or break fee. Watch for regulatory approvals and shareholder votes; risk-arb spreads may reflect integration complexity as a stock-for-stock merger of regional banks.

DIOD.brief: Diodes Incorporated (DIOD) filed an 8-K announcing its entry into a definitive merger agreement to acquire Elevate Semiconductor, Inc. for a base purchase price of $250.0 million in cash, subject to customary adjustments, plus up to $50.0 million in earnout payments based on 2027–2030 revenue and gross margin thresholds. The transaction will be effected via a merger of a wholly owned subsidiary into Elevate, with Elevate surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary. Each share of Elevate common stock will be converted into the right to receive cash; in-the-money vested options will be canceled for cash, while unvested options are canceled without consideration. Closing is subject to HSR Act clearance, absence of a material adverse effect, and other customary conditions. Watch for regulatory timing and any competing bid.

FBNC.brief: First Bancorp filed an 8-K regarding a definitive merger agreement to acquire First Carolina Bancshares for aggregate consideration of ~$166 million, or $64.22 per share, composed of 14.5340 shares of First Bancorp common stock plus $294.94 cash per share. Both boards unanimously approved the deal, which is expected to close in Q4 2026 or early Q1 2027, pending First Carolina shareholder approval, regulatory clearances, and effectiveness of a registration statement. A June 30, 2027 termination date applies. Watch for regulatory approvals and shareholder vote for risk-arb spreads.

ARCB.brief: ArcBest Corporation announced a restructuring plan on July 16, 2026 via Form 8-K, involving a ~2% workforce reduction, consolidation of brands (MoLo, Panther, ArcBest Technologies under the ArcBest brand), closure of ten ABF Freight service centers (~1% of doors), and discontinuation of the Vaux Freight Movement System. Estimated cash charges of $6-7 million (primarily Q3 2026) and non-cash impairments of ~$76.5 million (recognized in Q2 2026). Facility consolidations require union-management committee approval per the NMFA. Watch for Q2 impairment impact and union negotiation outcomes.

UBER.brief: Uber Technologies filed an 8-K on July 16, 2026, announcing a Business Combination Agreement to launch a voluntary public takeover offer for Delivery Hero SE (a German Societas Europaea) via its subsidiary Bidder. The Offer is for all Delivery Hero shares at €41.50 per share in cash (implied value not disclosed). The Delivery Hero management and supervisory boards unanimously recommend acceptance, subject to fiduciary duties. The transaction requires regulatory approvals and a minimum tender condition; completion is expected in H2 2027. Post-offer, Delivery Hero will become a majority-owned indirect subsidiary of Uber. Watch: regulatory clearances and shareholder tender response.

IPGP.brief: IPG Photonics Corp filed an 8-K regarding a Put Option Agreement with Lumibird S.A. to acquire 100% of Lumibird Medical for €300 million on a cash-free, debt-free basis, payable at closing in cash, plus up to €50 million contingent earnout based on 2026-2027 performance. The acquisition is to be funded from cash on hand. The put option remains exercisable after consultation with the French works council and expires 10 business days post-consultation or after six months. A €3.5M reverse break fee applies if Lumibird fails to exercise. Watch for regulatory clearance and the earnout milestones for risk-arb analysis.

PENG.brief: Penguin Solutions filed an 8-K disclosing the issuance of $750M (plus $100M greenshoe) of 0.00% convertible senior notes due 2031. Net proceeds of ~$735.1M are used to repurchase $135.5M of its 2.00% 2029 notes and $160M of its 2.00% 2030 notes, pay $49.1M for capped call transactions, repay $100M of a credit facility, and for general corporate purposes. The notes are zero-coupon, mature August 1, 2031, and convertible into cash and possibly shares. The transaction refinances existing debt and reduces interest expense. No board recommendation or advisor named. Watch for dilutive conversion overhang and share price action relative to conversion price.

CBRL.company: CRACKER BARREL OLD COUNTRY STORE, INC
CBRL.brief: Cracker Barrel filed an 8-K reporting a sale-leaseback of 26 properties to an institutional investor for ~$77M net proceeds, used to repay credit facility debt, and a separate divestiture of its MSBC business (unspecified terms). The leases are triple-net with a 40-year max term, initial annual rent ~$5.7M subject to fixed increases, and the company exited/closed the MSBC operations, recording impairment and exit costs. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The sale-leaseback mimics a financing transaction rather than a core divestiture; however, the MSBC sale is a clear divestiture. Watch for future asset sales or restructuring as the company reduces debt and refocuses.

LXP.brief: LXP Industrial Trust filed an 8-K announcing a definitive merger agreement to be acquired by Leopard REIT LLC, a vehicle controlled by an unnamed parent, in a going-private transaction. Each common share will be cancelled and converted into the right to receive cash, though exact per-share price, premium, and implied value are not disclosed in this excerpt. The board unanimously approved the merger and recommends common shareholder approval at a special meeting. Series C preferred shares remain outstanding. The transaction is subject to shareholder vote, regulatory approvals, and customary closing conditions. The acquiring entity is a newly formed LLC, suggesting sponsor-backed take-private. Watch for financing details and shareholder vote timeline; risk-arb spread depends on disclosed consideration.

MGY.brief: Magnolia Oil & Gas Corp filed an 8-K reporting its entry into a purchase agreement to acquire 100% of WildFire Intermediate Holdings (Target) from WildFire Energy I LLC. Consideration comprises $2.65 billion cash, 32,203,000 shares of Magnolia Class A common stock, and assumption of $600 million of Target's 7.500% Senior Notes due 2029. The board recommendation was not specified; no advisors were named. Closing is subject to HSR clearance and customary conditions. A $200 million escrow deposit secures performance. Watch for antitrust review timelines and financing risk-arb spread on the cash-and-stock mix.

CFG.brief: Citizens Financial Group filed an 8-K announcing a proposed public offering of new Series J Fixed-Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock. Proceeds, if the offering closes, would redeem some or all of its outstanding Series G Preferred Stock ($1,000 liquidation preference). Pricing and closing are subject to market conditions; no terms, premium, or board recommendation are provided. This is a liability management capital transaction, not a special situation like a tender offer or going-private. Watch for pricing terms and a subsequent redemption announcement.

HMN.brief: Horace Mann Educators Corporation filed an 8-K reporting its entry into a Membership Interest Purchase Agreement to acquire all equity interests of Employee Services LLC from Medical Mutual of Ohio for approximately $115 million cash, funded by cash on hand and borrowings under its existing credit facility. The board approved the deal. Closing is expected in Q4 2026, subject to conditions. This is an acquisition of a business (ESI). Watch for regulatory approvals and integration risk; no public premium or stake size specified as ESI is private.
